16517.label: Proverbs 1:1
16517.text: The proverbs of Solʹo·mon the son of David, the king of Israel,

16518.label: Proverbs 1:2
16518.text: for one to know wisdom and discipline, to discern the sayings of understanding,

16519.label: Proverbs 1:3
16519.text: to receive the discipline that gives insight, righteousness and judgment and uprightness,

16520.label: Proverbs 1:4
16520.text: to give to the inexperienced ones shrewdness, to a young man knowledge and thinking ability.

16521.label: Proverbs 1:5
16521.text: A wise person will listen and take in more instruction, and a man of understanding is the one who acquires skillful direction,

16522.label: Proverbs 1:6
16522.text: to understand a proverb and a puzzling saying, the words of wise persons and their riddles.

16523.label: Proverbs 1:7
16523.text: The fear of Jehovah is the beginning of knowledge. Wisdom and discipline are what mere fools have despised.

16524.label: Proverbs 1:8
16524.text: Listen, my son, to the discipline of your father, and do not forsake the law of your mother.

16525.label: Proverbs 1:9
16525.text: For they are a wreath of attractiveness to your head and a fine necklace to your throat.

16526.label: Proverbs 1:10
16526.text: My son, if sinners try to seduce you, do not consent.

16527.label: Proverbs 1:11
16527.text: If they keep saying: “Do go with us. Do let us lie in ambush for blood. Do let us lie in concealment for the innocent men without any cause.

16528.label: Proverbs 1:12
16528.text: Let us swallow them down alive just like Sheʹol, even whole, like those going down into a pit.

16529.label: Proverbs 1:13
16529.text: Let us find all sorts of precious valuables. Let us fill our houses with spoil.

16530.label: Proverbs 1:14
16530.text: Your lot you ought to cast in among us. Let there come to be just one bag belonging to all of us” —

16531.label: Proverbs 1:15
16531.text: my son, do not go in the way with them. Hold back your foot from their roadway.

16532.label: Proverbs 1:16
16532.text: For their feet are those that run to sheer badness, and they keep hastening to shed blood.

16533.label: Proverbs 1:17
16533.text: For it is for nothing that the net is spread before the eyes of anything owning wings.

16534.label: Proverbs 1:18
16534.text: Consequently they themselves lie in ambush for the very blood of these; they lie in concealment for their souls.

16535.label: Proverbs 1:19
16535.text: Thus are the paths of everyone making unjust profit. It takes away the very soul of its owners.

16536.label: Proverbs 1:20
16536.text: True wisdom itself keeps crying aloud in the very street. In the public squares it keeps giving forth its voice.

16537.label: Proverbs 1:21
16537.text: At the upper end of the noisy streets it calls out. At the entrances of the gates into the city it says its own sayings:

16538.label: Proverbs 1:22
16538.text: “How long will YOU inexperienced ones keep loving inexperience, and [how long] must YOU ridiculers desire for yourselves outright ridicule, and [how long] will YOU stupid ones keep hating knowledge?

16539.label: Proverbs 1:23
16539.text: Turn back at my reproof. Then to YOU I will cause my spirit to bubble forth; I will make my words known to YOU.

16540.label: Proverbs 1:24
16540.text: Because I have called out but YOU keep refusing, I have stretched out my hand but there is no one paying attention,

16541.label: Proverbs 1:25
16541.text: and YOU keep neglecting all my counsel, and my reproof YOU have not accepted,

16542.label: Proverbs 1:26
16542.text: I also, for my part, shall laugh at YOUR own disaster, I shall mock when what YOU dread comes,

16543.label: Proverbs 1:27
16543.text: when what YOU dread comes just like a storm, and YOUR own disaster gets here just like a storm wind, when distress and hard times come upon YOU.

16544.label: Proverbs 1:28
16544.text: At that time they will keep calling me, but I shall not answer; they will keep looking for me, but they will not find me,

16545.label: Proverbs 1:29
16545.text: for the reason that they hated knowledge, and the fear of Jehovah they did not choose.

16546.label: Proverbs 1:30
16546.text: They did not consent to my counsel; they disrespected all my reproof.

16547.label: Proverbs 1:31
16547.text: So they will eat from the fruitage of their way, and they will be glutted with their own counsels.

16548.label: Proverbs 1:32
16548.text: For the renegading of the inexperienced ones is what will kill them, and the easygoingness of the stupid is what will destroy them.

16549.label: Proverbs 1:33
16549.text: As for the one listening to me, he will reside in security and be undisturbed from dread of calamity.”

16550.label: Proverbs 2:1
16550.text: My son, if you will receive my sayings and treasure up my own commandments with yourself,

16551.label: Proverbs 2:2
16551.text: so as to pay attention to wisdom with your ear, that you may incline your heart to discernment;

16552.label: Proverbs 2:3
16552.text: if, moreover, you call out for understanding itself and you give forth your voice for discernment itself,

16553.label: Proverbs 2:4
16553.text: if you keep seeking for it as for silver, and as for hid treasures you keep searching for it,

16554.label: Proverbs 2:5
16554.text: in that case you will understand the fear of Jehovah, and you will find the very knowledge of God.

16555.label: Proverbs 2:6
16555.text: For Jehovah himself gives wisdom; out of his mouth there are knowledge and discernment.

16556.label: Proverbs 2:7
16556.text: And for the upright ones he will treasure up practical wisdom; for those walking in integrity he is a shield,

16557.label: Proverbs 2:8
16557.text: by observing the paths of judgment, and he will guard the very way of his loyal ones.

16558.label: Proverbs 2:9
16558.text: In that case you will understand righteousness and judgment and uprightness, the entire course of what is good.

16559.label: Proverbs 2:10
16559.text: When wisdom enters into your heart and knowledge itself becomes pleasant to your very soul,

16560.label: Proverbs 2:11
16560.text: thinking ability itself will keep guard over you, discernment itself will safeguard you,

16561.label: Proverbs 2:12
16561.text: to deliver you from the bad way, from the man speaking perverse things,

16562.label: Proverbs 2:13
16562.text: from those leaving the paths of uprightness to walk in the ways of darkness,

16563.label: Proverbs 2:14
16563.text: from those who are rejoicing in doing bad, who are joyful in the perverse things of badness;

16564.label: Proverbs 2:15
16564.text: those whose paths are crooked and who are devious in their general course;

16565.label: Proverbs 2:16
16565.text: to deliver you from the strange woman, from the foreign woman who has made her own sayings smooth,

16566.label: Proverbs 2:17
16566.text: who is leaving the confidential friend of her youth and who has forgotten the very covenant of her God.

16567.label: Proverbs 2:18
16567.text: For down to death her house does sink and down to those impotent in death her tracks.

16568.label: Proverbs 2:19
16568.text: None of those having relations with her will come back, nor will they regain the paths of those living.

16569.label: Proverbs 2:20
16569.text: The purpose is that you may walk in the way of good people and that the paths of the righteous ones you may keep.

16570.label: Proverbs 2:21
16570.text: For the upright are the ones that will reside in the earth, and the blameless are the ones that will be left over in it.

16571.label: Proverbs 2:22
16571.text: As regards the wicked, they will be cut off from the very earth; and as for the treacherous, they will be torn away from it.

16572.label: Proverbs 3:1
16572.text: My son, my law do not forget, and my commandments may your heart observe,

16573.label: Proverbs 3:2
16573.text: because length of days and years of life and peace will be added to you.

16574.label: Proverbs 3:3
16574.text: May loving-kindness and trueness themselves not leave you. Tie them about your throat. Write them upon the tablet of your heart,

16575.label: Proverbs 3:4
16575.text: and so find favor and good insight in the eyes of God and of earthling man.

16576.label: Proverbs 3:5
16576.text: Trust in Jehovah with all your heart and do not lean upon your own understanding.

16577.label: Proverbs 3:6
16577.text: In all your ways take notice of him, and he himself will make your paths straight.

16578.label: Proverbs 3:7
16578.text: Do not become wise in your own eyes. Fear Jehovah and turn away from bad.

16579.label: Proverbs 3:8
16579.text: May it become a healing to your navel and a refreshment to your bones.

16580.label: Proverbs 3:9
16580.text: Honor Jehovah with your valuable things and with the firstfruits of all your produce.

16581.label: Proverbs 3:10
16581.text: Then your stores of supply will be filled with plenty; and with new wine your own press vats will overflow.

16582.label: Proverbs 3:11
16582.text: The discipline of Jehovah, O my son, do not reject; and do not abhor his reproof,

16583.label: Proverbs 3:12
16583.text: because the one whom Jehovah loves he reproves, even as a father does a son in whom he finds pleasure.

16584.label: Proverbs 3:13
16584.text: Happy is the man that has found wisdom, and the man that gets discernment,

16585.label: Proverbs 3:14
16585.text: for having it as gain is better than having silver as gain and having it as produce than gold itself.

16586.label: Proverbs 3:15
16586.text: It is more precious than corals, and all other delights of yours cannot be made equal to it.

16587.label: Proverbs 3:16
16587.text: Length of days is in its right hand; in its left hand there are riches and glory.

16588.label: Proverbs 3:17
16588.text: Its ways are ways of pleasantness, and all its roadways are peace.

16589.label: Proverbs 3:18
16589.text: It is a tree of life to those taking hold of it, and those keeping fast hold of it are to be called happy.

16590.label: Proverbs 3:19
16590.text: Jehovah himself in wisdom founded the earth. He solidly fixed the heavens in discernment.

16591.label: Proverbs 3:20
16591.text: By his knowledge the watery deeps themselves were split apart, and the cloudy skies keep dripping down light rain.

16592.label: Proverbs 3:21
16592.text: My son, may they not get away from your eyes. Safeguard practical wisdom and thinking ability,

16593.label: Proverbs 3:22
16593.text: and they will prove to be life to your soul and charm to your throat.

16594.label: Proverbs 3:23
16594.text: In that case you will walk in security on your way, and even your foot will not strike against anything.

16595.label: Proverbs 3:24
16595.text: Whenever you lie down you will feel no dread; and you will certainly lie down, and your sleep must be pleasurable.

16596.label: Proverbs 3:25
16596.text: You will not need to be afraid of any sudden dreadful thing, nor of the storm upon the wicked ones, because it is coming.

16597.label: Proverbs 3:26
16597.text: For Jehovah himself will prove to be, in effect, your confidence, and he will certainly keep your foot against capture.

16598.label: Proverbs 3:27
16598.text: Do not hold back good from those to whom it is owing, when it happens to be in the power of your hand to do [it].

16599.label: Proverbs 3:28
16599.text: Do not say to your fellowman: “Go, and come back and tomorrow I shall give,” when there is something with you.

16600.label: Proverbs 3:29
16600.text: Do not fabricate against your fellowman anything bad, when he is dwelling in a sense of security with you.

16601.label: Proverbs 3:30
16601.text: Do not quarrel with a man without cause, if he has rendered no bad to you.

16602.label: Proverbs 3:31
16602.text: Do not become envious of the man of violence, nor choose any of his ways.

16603.label: Proverbs 3:32
16603.text: For the devious person is a detestable thing to Jehovah, but His intimacy is with the upright ones.

16604.label: Proverbs 3:33
16604.text: The curse of Jehovah is on the house of the wicked one, but the abiding place of the righteous ones he blesses.

16605.label: Proverbs 3:34
16605.text: If it has to do with ridiculers, he himself will deride; but to the meek ones he will show favor.

16606.label: Proverbs 3:35
16606.text: Honor is what the wise ones will come to possess, but the stupid ones are exalting dishonor.

16607.label: Proverbs 4:1
16607.text: Listen, O sons, to the discipline of a father and pay attention, so as to know understanding.

16608.label: Proverbs 4:2
16608.text: For good instruction is what I certainly shall give to YOU. My law DO not leave.

16609.label: Proverbs 4:3
16609.text: For I proved to be a real son to my father, tender and the only one before my mother.

16610.label: Proverbs 4:4
16610.text: And he would instruct me and say to me: “May your heart keep fast hold of my words. Keep my commandments and continue living.

16611.label: Proverbs 4:5
16611.text: Acquire wisdom, acquire understanding. Do not forget, and do not turn aside from the sayings of my mouth.

16612.label: Proverbs 4:6
16612.text: Do not leave it, and it will keep you. Love it, and it will safeguard you.

16613.label: Proverbs 4:7
16613.text: Wisdom is the prime thing. Acquire wisdom; and with all that you acquire, acquire understanding.

16614.label: Proverbs 4:8
16614.text: Highly esteem it, and it will exalt you. It will glorify you because you embrace it.

16615.label: Proverbs 4:9
16615.text: To your head it will give a wreath of charm; a crown of beauty it will bestow upon you.”

16616.label: Proverbs 4:10
16616.text: Hear, my son, and accept my sayings. Then for you the years of life will become many.

16617.label: Proverbs 4:11
16617.text: I will instruct you even in the way of wisdom; I will cause you to tread in the tracks of uprightness.

16618.label: Proverbs 4:12
16618.text: When you walk, your pace will not be cramped; and if you run, you will not stumble.

16619.label: Proverbs 4:13
16619.text: Take hold on discipline; do not let go. Safeguard it, for it itself is your life.

16620.label: Proverbs 4:14
16620.text: Into the path of the wicked ones do not enter, and do not walk straight on into the way of the bad ones.

16621.label: Proverbs 4:15
16621.text: Shun it, do not pass along by it; turn aside from it, and pass along.

16622.label: Proverbs 4:16
16622.text: For they do not sleep unless they do badness, and their sleep has been snatched away unless they cause someone to stumble.

16623.label: Proverbs 4:17
16623.text: For they have fed themselves with the bread of wickedness, and the wine of acts of violence is what they drink.

16624.label: Proverbs 4:18
16624.text: But the path of the righteous ones is like the bright light that is getting lighter and lighter until the day is firmly established.

16625.label: Proverbs 4:19
16625.text: The way of the wicked ones is like the gloom; they have not known at what they keep stumbling.

16626.label: Proverbs 4:20
16626.text: My son, to my words do pay attention. To my sayings incline your ear.

16627.label: Proverbs 4:21
16627.text: May they not get away from your eyes. Keep them in the midst of your heart.

16628.label: Proverbs 4:22
16628.text: For they are life to those finding them and health to all their flesh.

16629.label: Proverbs 4:23
16629.text: More than all else that is to be guarded, safeguard your heart, for out of it are the sources of life.

16630.label: Proverbs 4:24
16630.text: Remove from yourself the crookedness of speech; and the deviousness of lips put far away from yourself.

16631.label: Proverbs 4:25
16631.text: As for your eyes, straight ahead they should look, yes, your own beaming eyes should gaze straight in front of you.

16632.label: Proverbs 4:26
16632.text: Smooth out the course of your foot, and may all your own ways be firmly established.

16633.label: Proverbs 4:27
16633.text: Do not incline to the right hand or to the left. Remove your foot from what is bad.

16634.label: Proverbs 5:1
16634.text: My son, to my wisdom O do pay attention. To my discernment incline your ears,

16635.label: Proverbs 5:2
16635.text: so as to guard thinking abilities; and may your own lips safeguard knowledge itself.

16636.label: Proverbs 5:3
16636.text: For as a honeycomb the lips of a strange woman keep dripping, and her palate is smoother than oil.

16637.label: Proverbs 5:4
16637.text: But the aftereffect from her is as bitter as wormwood; it is as sharp as a two-edged sword.

16638.label: Proverbs 5:5
16638.text: Her feet are descending to death. Her very steps take hold on Sheʹol itself.

16639.label: Proverbs 5:6
16639.text: The path of life she does not contemplate. Her tracks have wandered she does not know [where].

16640.label: Proverbs 5:7
16640.text: So now, O sons, listen to me and do not turn away from the sayings of my mouth.

16641.label: Proverbs 5:8
16641.text: Keep your way far off from alongside her, and do not get near to the entrance of her house,

16642.label: Proverbs 5:9
16642.text: that you may not give to others your dignity, nor your years to what is cruel;

16643.label: Proverbs 5:10
16643.text: that strangers may not satisfy themselves with your power, nor the things you got by pain be in the house of a foreigner,

16644.label: Proverbs 5:11
16644.text: nor you have to groan in your future when your flesh and your organism come to an end.

16645.label: Proverbs 5:12
16645.text: And you will have to say: “How I have hated discipline and my heart has disrespected even reproof!

16646.label: Proverbs 5:13
16646.text: And I have not listened to the voice of my instructors, and to my teachers I have not inclined my ear.

16647.label: Proverbs 5:14
16647.text: Easily I have come to be in every sort of badness in the midst of the congregation and of the assembly.”

16648.label: Proverbs 5:15
16648.text: Drink water out of your own cistern, and tricklings out of the midst of your own well.

16649.label: Proverbs 5:16
16649.text: Should your springs be scattered out of doors, [your] streams of water in the public squares themselves?

16650.label: Proverbs 5:17
16650.text: Let them prove to be for you alone, and not for strangers with you.

16651.label: Proverbs 5:18
16651.text: Let your water source prove to be blessed, and rejoice with the wife of your youth,

16652.label: Proverbs 5:19
16652.text: a lovable hind and a charming mountain goat. Let her own breasts intoxicate you at all times. With her love may you be in an ecstasy constantly.

16653.label: Proverbs 5:20
16653.text: So why should you, my son, be in an ecstasy with a strange woman or embrace the bosom of a foreign woman?

16654.label: Proverbs 5:21
16654.text: For the ways of man are in front of the eyes of Jehovah, and he is contemplating all his tracks.

16655.label: Proverbs 5:22
16655.text: His own errors will catch the wicked one, and in the ropes of his own sin he will be taken hold of.

16656.label: Proverbs 5:23
16656.text: He will be the one to die because there is no discipline, and [because] in the abundance of his foolishness he goes astray.

16657.label: Proverbs 6:1
16657.text: My son, if you have gone surety for your fellowman, [if] you have given your handshake even to the stranger,

16658.label: Proverbs 6:2
16658.text: [if] you have been ensnared by the sayings of your mouth, [if] you have been caught by the sayings of your mouth,

16659.label: Proverbs 6:3
16659.text: take this action then, my son, and deliver yourself, for you have come into the palm of your fellowman: Go humble yourself and storm your fellowman with importunities.

16660.label: Proverbs 6:4
16660.text: Do not give any sleep to your eyes, nor any slumber to your beaming eyes.

16661.label: Proverbs 6:5
16661.text: Deliver yourself like a gazelle from the hand and like a bird from the hand of the birdcatcher.

16662.label: Proverbs 6:6
16662.text: Go to the ant, you lazy one; see its ways and become wise.

16663.label: Proverbs 6:7
16663.text: Although it has no commander, officer or ruler,

16664.label: Proverbs 6:8
16664.text: it prepares its food even in the summer; it has gathered its food supplies even in the harvest.

16665.label: Proverbs 6:9
16665.text: How long, you lazy one, will you keep lying down? When will you rise up from your sleep?

16666.label: Proverbs 6:10
16666.text: A little more sleep, a little more slumbering, a little more folding of the hands in lying down,

16667.label: Proverbs 6:11
16667.text: and your poverty will certainly come just like some rover, and your want like an armed man.

16668.label: Proverbs 6:12
16668.text: A good-for-nothing man, a man of hurtfulness, is walking with crookedness of speech,

16669.label: Proverbs 6:13
16669.text: winking with his eye, making signs with his foot, making indications with his fingers.

16670.label: Proverbs 6:14
16670.text: Perverseness is in his heart. He is fabricating something bad all the time. He keeps sending out merely contentions.

16671.label: Proverbs 6:15
16671.text: That is why suddenly there will come his disaster; in an instant he will be broken, and there will be no healing.

16672.label: Proverbs 6:16
16672.text: There are six things that Jehovah does hate; yes, seven are things detestable to his soul:

16673.label: Proverbs 6:17
16673.text: lofty eyes, a false tongue, and hands that are shedding innocent blood,

16674.label: Proverbs 6:18
16674.text: a heart fabricating hurtful schemes, feet that are in a hurry to run to badness,

16675.label: Proverbs 6:19
16675.text: a false witness that launches forth lies, and anyone sending forth contentions among brothers.

16676.label: Proverbs 6:20
16676.text: Observe, O my son, the commandment of your father, and do not forsake the law of your mother.

16677.label: Proverbs 6:21
16677.text: Tie them upon your heart constantly; bind them upon your throat.

16678.label: Proverbs 6:22
16678.text: When you walk about, it will lead you; when you lie down, it will stand guard over you; and when you have waked up, it itself will make you its concern.

16679.label: Proverbs 6:23
16679.text: For the commandment is a lamp, and a light the law is, and the reproofs of discipline are the way of life,

16680.label: Proverbs 6:24
16680.text: to guard you against the bad woman, against the smoothness of the tongue of the foreign woman.

16681.label: Proverbs 6:25
16681.text: Do not desire her prettiness in your heart, and may she not take you with her lustrous eyes,

16682.label: Proverbs 6:26
16682.text: because in behalf of a woman prostitute [one comes down] to a round loaf of bread; but as regards another man’s wife, she hunts even for a precious soul.

16683.label: Proverbs 6:27
16683.text: Can a man rake together fire into his bosom and yet his very garments not be burned?

16684.label: Proverbs 6:28
16684.text: Or can a man walk upon the coals and his feet themselves not be scorched?

16685.label: Proverbs 6:29
16685.text: Likewise with anyone having relations with the wife of his fellowman, no one touching her will remain unpunishable.

16686.label: Proverbs 6:30
16686.text: People do not despise a thief just because he commits thievery to fill his soul when he is hungry.

16687.label: Proverbs 6:31
16687.text: But, when found, he will make it good with seven times as much; all the valuables of his house he will give.

16688.label: Proverbs 6:32
16688.text: Anyone committing adultery with a woman is in want of heart; he that does it is bringing his own soul to ruin.

16689.label: Proverbs 6:33
16689.text: A plague and dishonor he will find, and his reproach itself will not be wiped out.

16690.label: Proverbs 6:34
16690.text: For the rage of an able-bodied man is jealousy, and he will not show compassion in the day of vengeance.

16691.label: Proverbs 6:35
16691.text: He will have no consideration for any sort of ransom, neither will he show willingness, no matter how large you make the present.

16692.label: Proverbs 7:1
16692.text: My son, keep my sayings, and may you treasure up my own commandments with you.

16693.label: Proverbs 7:2
16693.text: Keep my commandments and continue living, and my law like the pupil of your eyes.

16694.label: Proverbs 7:3
16694.text: Tie them upon your fingers, and write them upon the tablet of your heart.

16695.label: Proverbs 7:4
16695.text: Say to wisdom: “You are my sister”; and may you call understanding itself “Kinswoman,”

16696.label: Proverbs 7:5
16696.text: to guard you against the woman stranger, against the foreigner who has made her own sayings smooth.

16697.label: Proverbs 7:6
16697.text: For at the window of my house, through my lattice I looked down,

16698.label: Proverbs 7:7
16698.text: that I might peer upon the inexperienced ones. I was interested in discerning among the sons a young man in want of heart,

16699.label: Proverbs 7:8
16699.text: passing along on the street near her corner, and in the way to her house he marches,

16700.label: Proverbs 7:9
16700.text: in the twilight, in the evening of the day, at the approach of the night and the gloom.

16701.label: Proverbs 7:10
16701.text: And, look! there was a woman to meet him, with the garment of a prostitute and cunning of heart.

16702.label: Proverbs 7:11
16702.text: She is boisterous and stubborn. In her house her feet do not keep residing.

16703.label: Proverbs 7:12
16703.text: Now she is outdoors, now she is in the public squares, and near every corner she lies in wait.

16704.label: Proverbs 7:13
16704.text: And she has grabbed hold of him and given him a kiss. She has put on a bold face, and she begins to say to him:

16705.label: Proverbs 7:14
16705.text: “Communion sacrifices were incumbent upon me. Today I have paid my vows.

16706.label: Proverbs 7:15
16706.text: That is why I have come out to meet you, to look for your face, that I may find you.

16707.label: Proverbs 7:16
16707.text: With coverlets I have bedecked my divan, with many-colored things, linen of Egypt.

16708.label: Proverbs 7:17
16708.text: I have besprinkled my bed with myrrh, aloes and cinnamon.

16709.label: Proverbs 7:18
16709.text: Do come, let us drink our fill of love until the morning; do let us enjoy each other with love expressions.

16710.label: Proverbs 7:19
16710.text: For the husband is not in his house; he has gone traveling on a way of some distance.

16711.label: Proverbs 7:20
16711.text: A bag of money he has taken in his hand. On the day of the full moon he will come to his house.”

16712.label: Proverbs 7:21
16712.text: She has misled him by the abundance of her persuasiveness. By the smoothness of her lips she seduces him.

16713.label: Proverbs 7:22
16713.text: All of a sudden he is going after her, like a bull that comes even to the slaughter, and just as if fettered for the discipline of a foolish man,

16714.label: Proverbs 7:23
16714.text: until an arrow cleaves open his liver, just as a bird hastens into the trap, and he has not known that it involves his very soul.

16715.label: Proverbs 7:24
16715.text: And now, O sons, listen to me and pay attention to the sayings of my mouth.

16716.label: Proverbs 7:25
16716.text: May your heart not turn aside to her ways. Do not wander into her roadways.

16717.label: Proverbs 7:26
16717.text: For many are the ones she has caused to fall down slain, and all those being killed by her are numerous.

16718.label: Proverbs 7:27
16718.text: The ways to Sheʹol her house is; they are descending to the interior rooms of death.

16719.label: Proverbs 8:1
16719.text: Does not wisdom keep calling out, and discernment keep giving forth its voice?

16720.label: Proverbs 8:2
16720.text: On top of the heights, by the way, at the crossing of the roadways it has stationed itself.

16721.label: Proverbs 8:3
16721.text: At the side of the gates, at the mouth of the town, at the going in of the entrances it keeps crying loudly:

16722.label: Proverbs 8:4
16722.text: “To YOU, O men, I am calling, and my voice is to the sons of men.

16723.label: Proverbs 8:5
16723.text: O inexperienced ones, understand shrewdness; and YOU stupid ones, understand heart.

16724.label: Proverbs 8:6
16724.text: Listen, for it is about the foremost things that I speak, and the opening of my lips is about uprightness.

16725.label: Proverbs 8:7
16725.text: For my palate in low tones utters truth itself; and wickedness is something detestable to my lips.

16726.label: Proverbs 8:8
16726.text: All the sayings of my mouth are in righteousness. Among them there is nothing twisted or crooked.

16727.label: Proverbs 8:9
16727.text: All of them are straight to the discerning one, and upright to the ones finding knowledge.

16728.label: Proverbs 8:10
16728.text: TAKE my discipline and not silver, and knowledge rather than choice gold.

16729.label: Proverbs 8:11
16729.text: For wisdom is better than corals, and all other delights themselves cannot be made equal to it.

16730.label: Proverbs 8:12
16730.text: “I, wisdom, I have resided with shrewdness and I find even the knowledge of thinking abilities.

16731.label: Proverbs 8:13
16731.text: The fear of Jehovah means the hating of bad. Self-exaltation and pride and the bad way and the perverse mouth I have hated.

16732.label: Proverbs 8:14
16732.text: I have counsel and practical wisdom. I—understanding; I have mightiness.

16733.label: Proverbs 8:15
16733.text: By me kings themselves keep reigning, and high officials themselves keep decreeing righteousness.

16734.label: Proverbs 8:16
16734.text: By me princes themselves keep ruling as princes, and nobles are all judging in righteousness.

16735.label: Proverbs 8:17
16735.text: Those loving me I myself love, and those looking for me are the ones that find me.

16736.label: Proverbs 8:18
16736.text: Riches and glory are with me, hereditary values and righteousness.

16737.label: Proverbs 8:19
16737.text: My fruitage is better than gold, even than refined gold, and my produce than choice silver.

16738.label: Proverbs 8:20
16738.text: In the path of righteousness I walk, in the middle of the roadways of judgment,

16739.label: Proverbs 8:21
16739.text: to cause those loving me to take possession of substance; and their storehouses I keep filled.

16740.label: Proverbs 8:22
16740.text: “Jehovah himself produced me as the beginning of his way, the earliest of his achievements of long ago.

16741.label: Proverbs 8:23
16741.text: From time indefinite I was installed, from the start, from times earlier than the earth.

16742.label: Proverbs 8:24
16742.text: When there were no watery deeps I was brought forth as with labor pains, when there were no springs heavily charged with water.

16743.label: Proverbs 8:25
16743.text: Before the mountains themselves had been settled down, ahead of the hills, I was brought forth as with labor pains,

16744.label: Proverbs 8:26
16744.text: when as yet he had not made the earth and the open spaces and the first part of the dust masses of the productive land.

16745.label: Proverbs 8:27
16745.text: When he prepared the heavens I was there; when he decreed a circle upon the face of the watery deep,

16746.label: Proverbs 8:28
16746.text: when he made firm the cloud masses above, when he caused the fountains of the watery deep to be strong,

16747.label: Proverbs 8:29
16747.text: when he set for the sea his decree that the waters themselves should not pass beyond his order, when he decreed the foundations of the earth,

16748.label: Proverbs 8:30
16748.text: then I came to be beside him as a master worker, and I came to be the one he was specially fond of day by day, I being glad before him all the time,

16749.label: Proverbs 8:31
16749.text: being glad at the productive land of his earth, and the things I was fond of were with the sons of men.

16750.label: Proverbs 8:32
16750.text: “And now, O sons, listen to me; yes, happy are the ones that keep my very ways.

16751.label: Proverbs 8:33
16751.text: Listen to discipline and become wise, and do not show any neglect.

16752.label: Proverbs 8:34
16752.text: Happy is the man that is listening to me by keeping awake at my doors day by day, by watching at the posts of my entrances.

16753.label: Proverbs 8:35
16753.text: For the one finding me will certainly find life, and gets goodwill from Jehovah.

16754.label: Proverbs 8:36
16754.text: But the one missing me is doing violence to his soul; all those intensely hating me are the ones that do love death.”

16755.label: Proverbs 9:1
16755.text: True wisdom has built its house; it has hewn out its seven pillars.

16756.label: Proverbs 9:2
16756.text: It has organized its meat slaughtering; it has mixed its wine; more than that, it has set in order its table.

16757.label: Proverbs 9:3
16757.text: It has sent forth its lady attendants, that it may call out on top of the heights of the town:

16758.label: Proverbs 9:4
16758.text: “Whoever is inexperienced, let him turn aside here.” Whoever is in want of heart —she has said to him:

16759.label: Proverbs 9:5
16759.text: “Come, feed yourselves with my bread and share in drinking the wine that I have mixed.

16760.label: Proverbs 9:6
16760.text: Leave the inexperienced ones and keep living, and walk straight in the way of understanding.”

16761.label: Proverbs 9:7
16761.text: He that is correcting the ridiculer is taking to himself dishonor, and he that is giving a reproof to someone wicked—a defect in him.

16762.label: Proverbs 9:8
16762.text: Do not reprove a ridiculer, that he may not hate you. Give a reproof to a wise person and he will love you.

16763.label: Proverbs 9:9
16763.text: Give to a wise person and he will become still wiser. Impart knowledge to someone righteous and he will increase in learning.

16764.label: Proverbs 9:10
16764.text: The fear of Jehovah is the start of wisdom, and the knowledge of the Most Holy One is what understanding is.

16765.label: Proverbs 9:11
16765.text: For by me your days will become many, and to you years of life will be added.

16766.label: Proverbs 9:12
16766.text: If you have become wise, you have become wise in your own behalf; and if you have ridiculed, you will bear [it], just you alone.

16767.label: Proverbs 9:13
16767.text: A woman of stupidity is boisterous. She is simplemindedness itself and has come to know nothing whatever.

16768.label: Proverbs 9:14
16768.text: And she has seated herself at the entrance of her house, upon a seat, [in] the high places of the town,

16769.label: Proverbs 9:15
16769.text: to call out to those passing along the way, those who are going straight ahead on their paths:

16770.label: Proverbs 9:16
16770.text: “Whoever is inexperienced, let him turn aside here.” And whoever is in want of heart —she has also said to him:

16771.label: Proverbs 9:17
16771.text: “Stolen waters themselves are sweet, and bread [eaten] in secrecy—it is pleasant.”

16772.label: Proverbs 9:18
16772.text: But he has not come to know that those impotent in death are there, that those called in by her are in the low places of Sheʹol.

16773.label: Proverbs 10:1
16773.text: Proverbs of Solʹo·mon. A wise son is the one that makes a father rejoice, and a stupid son is the grief of his mother.

16774.label: Proverbs 10:2
16774.text: The treasures of the wicked one will be of no benefit, but righteousness is what will deliver from death.

16775.label: Proverbs 10:3
16775.text: Jehovah will not cause the soul of the righteous one to go hungry, but the craving of the wicked ones he will push away.

16776.label: Proverbs 10:4
16776.text: The one working with a slack hand will be of little means, but the hand of the diligent one is what will make one rich.

16777.label: Proverbs 10:5
16777.text: The son acting with insight is gathering during the summertime; the son acting shamefully is fast asleep during the harvest.

16778.label: Proverbs 10:6
16778.text: Blessings are for the head of the righteous one, but as regards the mouth of the wicked ones, it covers up violence.

16779.label: Proverbs 10:7
16779.text: The remembrance of the righteous one is due for a blessing, but the very name of the wicked ones will rot.

16780.label: Proverbs 10:8
16780.text: The one wise in heart will accept commandments, but the one foolish with his lips will be trodden down.

16781.label: Proverbs 10:9
16781.text: He that is walking in integrity will walk in security, but he that is making his ways crooked will make himself known.

16782.label: Proverbs 10:10
16782.text: The one winking his eye will give pain, and the one foolish with his lips will be trodden down.

16783.label: Proverbs 10:11
16783.text: The mouth of the righteous one is a source of life; but as regards the mouth of the wicked ones, it covers up violence.

16784.label: Proverbs 10:12
16784.text: Hatred is what stirs up contentions, but love covers over even all transgressions.

16785.label: Proverbs 10:13
16785.text: On the lips of the understanding person wisdom is found, but the rod is for the back of one in want of heart.

16786.label: Proverbs 10:14
16786.text: The wise are the ones that treasure up knowledge, but the mouth of the foolish one is near to ruin itself.

16787.label: Proverbs 10:15
16787.text: The valuable things of a rich man are his strong town. The ruin of the lowly ones is their poverty.

16788.label: Proverbs 10:16
16788.text: The activity of the righteous one results in life; the produce of the wicked one results in sin.

16789.label: Proverbs 10:17
16789.text: He that is holding to discipline is a path to life, but he that is leaving reproof is causing to wander.

16790.label: Proverbs 10:18
16790.text: Where there is one covering over hatred there are lips of falsehood, and the one bringing forth a bad report is stupid.

16791.label: Proverbs 10:19
16791.text: In the abundance of words there does not fail to be transgression, but the one keeping his lips in check is acting discreetly.

16792.label: Proverbs 10:20
16792.text: The tongue of the righteous one is choice silver; the heart of the wicked one is worth little.

16793.label: Proverbs 10:21
16793.text: The very lips of the righteous one keep pasturing many, but for want of heart the foolish themselves keep dying.

16794.label: Proverbs 10:22
16794.text: The blessing of Jehovah—that is what makes rich, and he adds no pain with it.

16795.label: Proverbs 10:23
16795.text: To the stupid one the carrying on of loose conduct is like sport, but wisdom is for the man of discernment.

16796.label: Proverbs 10:24
16796.text: The thing frightful to the wicked one—that is what will come to him; but the desire of the righteous ones will be granted.

16797.label: Proverbs 10:25
16797.text: As when the storm wind passes over, so the wicked one is no more; but the righteous one is a foundation to time indefinite.

16798.label: Proverbs 10:26
16798.text: As vinegar to the teeth and as smoke to the eyes, so the lazy man is to those sending him forth.

16799.label: Proverbs 10:27
16799.text: The very fear of Jehovah will add days, but the years themselves of the wicked ones will be cut short.

16800.label: Proverbs 10:28
16800.text: The expectation of the righteous ones is a rejoicing, but the very hope of the wicked ones will perish.

16801.label: Proverbs 10:29
16801.text: The way of Jehovah is a stronghold for the blameless one, but ruin is for the practicers of what is hurtful.

16802.label: Proverbs 10:30
16802.text: As for the righteous one, to time indefinite he will not be caused to stagger; but as for the wicked ones, they will not keep residing on the earth.

16803.label: Proverbs 10:31
16803.text: The mouth of the righteous one—it bears the fruit of wisdom, but the tongue of perverseness will be cut off.

16804.label: Proverbs 10:32
16804.text: The lips of the righteous one—they come to know goodwill, but the mouth of the wicked ones is perverseness.

16805.label: Proverbs 11:1
16805.text: A cheating pair of scales is something detestable to Jehovah, but a complete stone-weight is a pleasure to him.

16806.label: Proverbs 11:2
16806.text: Has presumptuousness come? Then dishonor will come; but wisdom is with the modest ones.

16807.label: Proverbs 11:3
16807.text: The integrity of the upright ones is what leads them, but distortion by those dealing treacherously will despoil them.

16808.label: Proverbs 11:4
16808.text: Valuable things will be of no benefit on the day of fury, but righteousness itself will deliver from death.

16809.label: Proverbs 11:5
16809.text: The righteousness of the blameless one is what will make his way straight, but in his own wickedness the wicked one will fall.

16810.label: Proverbs 11:6
16810.text: The righteousness of the upright ones is what will deliver them, but by their craving those dealing treacherously will themselves be caught.

16811.label: Proverbs 11:7
16811.text: When a wicked man dies, [his] hope perishes; and even expectation [based] on powerfulness has perished.

16812.label: Proverbs 11:8
16812.text: The righteous is the one rescued even from distress, and the wicked one comes in instead of him.

16813.label: Proverbs 11:9
16813.text: By [his] mouth the one who is an apostate brings his fellowman to ruin, but by knowledge are the righteous rescued.

16814.label: Proverbs 11:10
16814.text: Because of the goodness of the righteous ones a town is elated, but when the wicked ones perish there is a joyful cry.

16815.label: Proverbs 11:11
16815.text: Because of the blessing of the upright ones a town is exalted, but because of the mouth of the wicked ones it gets torn down.

16816.label: Proverbs 11:12
16816.text: The one in want of heart has despised his own fellowman, but the man of broad discernment is one that keeps silent.

16817.label: Proverbs 11:13
16817.text: The one walking about as a slanderer is uncovering confidential talk, but the one faithful in spirit is covering over a matter.

16818.label: Proverbs 11:14
16818.text: When there is no skillful direction, the people fall; but there is salvation in the multitude of counselors.

16819.label: Proverbs 11:15
16819.text: One will positively fare badly because he has gone surety for a stranger, but the one hating handshaking is keeping carefree.

16820.label: Proverbs 11:16
16820.text: A woman of charm is the one that takes hold of glory; but the tyrants, for their part, take hold of riches.

16821.label: Proverbs 11:17
16821.text: A man of loving-kindness is dealing rewardingly with his own soul, but the cruel person is bringing ostracism upon his own organism.

16822.label: Proverbs 11:18
16822.text: The wicked one is making false wages, but the one sowing righteousness, true earnings.

16823.label: Proverbs 11:19
16823.text: The one firmly standing for righteousness is in line for life, but the one chasing after what is bad is in line for his own death.

16824.label: Proverbs 11:20
16824.text: Those crooked at heart are something detestable to Jehovah, but the ones blameless in [their] way are a pleasure to him.

16825.label: Proverbs 11:21
16825.text: Though hand be to hand, a bad person will not go unpunished; but the offspring of the righteous ones will certainly escape.

16826.label: Proverbs 11:22
16826.text: As a gold nose ring in the snout of a pig, so is a woman that is pretty but that is turning away from sensibleness.

16827.label: Proverbs 11:23
16827.text: The desire of the righteous ones is surely good; the hope of the wicked ones is fury.

16828.label: Proverbs 11:24
16828.text: There exists the one that is scattering and yet is being increased; also the one that is keeping back from what is right, but it results only in want.

16829.label: Proverbs 11:25
16829.text: The generous soul will itself be made fat, and the one freely watering [others] will himself also be freely watered.

16830.label: Proverbs 11:26
16830.text: The one holding back grain—the populace will execrate him, but there is a blessing for the head of the one letting it be bought.

16831.label: Proverbs 11:27
16831.text: He that is looking for good will keep seeking goodwill; but as for the one searching for bad, it will come upon him.

16832.label: Proverbs 11:28
16832.text: The one trusting in his riches—he himself will fall; but just like foliage the righteous ones will flourish.

16833.label: Proverbs 11:29
16833.text: As for anyone bringing ostracism upon his own house, he will take possession of wind; and a foolish person will be a servant to the one wise in heart.

16834.label: Proverbs 11:30
16834.text: The fruitage of the righteous one is a tree of life, and he that is winning souls is wise.

16835.label: Proverbs 11:31
16835.text: Look! The righteous one—in the earth he will be rewarded. How much more should the wicked one and the sinner be!

16836.label: Proverbs 12:1
16836.text: A lover of discipline is a lover of knowledge, but a hater of reproof is unreasoning.

16837.label: Proverbs 12:2
16837.text: One that is good gets approval from Jehovah, but the man of [wicked] ideas he pronounces wicked.

16838.label: Proverbs 12:3
16838.text: No man will be firmly established by wickedness; but as for the root-foundation of the righteous ones, it will not be caused to stagger.

16839.label: Proverbs 12:4
16839.text: A capable wife is a crown to her owner, but as rottenness in his bones is she that acts shamefully.

16840.label: Proverbs 12:5
16840.text: The thoughts of the righteous ones are judgment; the steering by the wicked ones is deception.

16841.label: Proverbs 12:6
16841.text: The words of the wicked ones are a lying in wait for blood, but the mouth of the upright ones is what will deliver them.

16842.label: Proverbs 12:7
16842.text: There is an overthrowing of the wicked ones and they are no more, but the very house of the righteous ones will keep standing.

16843.label: Proverbs 12:8
16843.text: For his mouth of discretion a man will be praised, but one who is twisted at heart will come to be for contempt.

16844.label: Proverbs 12:9
16844.text: Better is the one lightly esteemed but having a servant than the one glorifying himself but in want of bread.

16845.label: Proverbs 12:10
16845.text: The righteous one is caring for the soul of his domestic animal, but the mercies of the wicked ones are cruel.

16846.label: Proverbs 12:11
16846.text: The one cultivating his ground will himself be satisfied with bread, but the one pursuing valueless things is in want of heart.

16847.label: Proverbs 12:12
16847.text: The wicked one has desired the netted prey of bad men; but as for the root of the righteous ones, it yields.

16848.label: Proverbs 12:13
16848.text: By the transgression of the lips the bad person is ensnared, but the righteous one gets out of distress.

16849.label: Proverbs 12:14
16849.text: From the fruitage of a man’s mouth he is satisfied with good, and the very doing of a man’s hands will come back to him.

16850.label: Proverbs 12:15
16850.text: The way of the foolish one is right in his own eyes, but the one listening to counsel is wise.

16851.label: Proverbs 12:16
16851.text: It is a foolish person that makes known his vexation in the [same] day, but the shrewd one is covering over a dishonor.

16852.label: Proverbs 12:17
16852.text: He that launches forth faithfulness will tell what is righteous, but a false witness, deception.

16853.label: Proverbs 12:18
16853.text: There exists the one speaking thoughtlessly as with the stabs of a sword, but the tongue of the wise ones is a healing.

16854.label: Proverbs 12:19
16854.text: It is the lip of truth that will be firmly established forever, but the tongue of falsehood will be only as long as a moment.

16855.label: Proverbs 12:20
16855.text: Deception is in the heart of those fabricating mischief, but those counseling peace have rejoicing.

16856.label: Proverbs 12:21
16856.text: Nothing hurtful will befall the righteous one, but the wicked are the ones that will certainly be filled with calamity.

16857.label: Proverbs 12:22
16857.text: False lips are something detestable to Jehovah, but those acting in faithfulness are a pleasure to him.

16858.label: Proverbs 12:23
16858.text: A shrewd man is covering knowledge, but the heart of the stupid ones is one that calls out foolishness.

16859.label: Proverbs 12:24
16859.text: The hand of the diligent ones is the one that will rule, but the slack hand will come to be for forced labor.

16860.label: Proverbs 12:25
16860.text: Anxious care in the heart of a man is what will cause it to bow down, but the good word is what makes it rejoice.

16861.label: Proverbs 12:26
16861.text: The righteous one spies out his own pasturage, but the very way of wicked ones causes them to wander about.

16862.label: Proverbs 12:27
16862.text: Slackness will not start up one’s game animals, but the diligent one is a man’s precious wealth.

16863.label: Proverbs 12:28
16863.text: In the path of righteousness there is life, and the journey in its pathway means no death.

16864.label: Proverbs 13:1
16864.text: A son is wise where there is a father’s discipline, but the ridiculer is one that has not heard rebuke.

16865.label: Proverbs 13:2
16865.text: From the fruitage of his mouth a man will eat good, but the very soul of those dealing treacherously is violence.

16866.label: Proverbs 13:3
16866.text: The one guarding his mouth is keeping his soul. The one opening wide his lips—he will have ruin.

16867.label: Proverbs 13:4
16867.text: The lazy one is showing himself desirous, but his soul [has] nothing. However, the very soul of the diligent ones will be made fat.

16868.label: Proverbs 13:5
16868.text: A false word is what the righteous hates, but the wicked ones act shamefully and cause disgrace for themselves.

16869.label: Proverbs 13:6
16869.text: Righteousness itself safeguards the one who is harmless in his way, but wickedness is what subverts the sinner.

16870.label: Proverbs 13:7
16870.text: There exists the one that is pretending to be rich and yet he has nothing at all; there is the one that is pretending to be of little means and yet [he has] many valuable things.

16871.label: Proverbs 13:8
16871.text: The ransom for a man’s soul is his riches, but the one of little means has not heard rebuke.

16872.label: Proverbs 13:9
16872.text: The very light of the righteous ones will rejoice; but the lamp of the wicked ones—it will be extinguished.

16873.label: Proverbs 13:10
16873.text: By presumptuousness one only causes a struggle, but with those consulting together there is wisdom.

16874.label: Proverbs 13:11
16874.text: Valuable things resulting from vanity become fewer, but the one collecting by the hand is the one that makes increase.

16875.label: Proverbs 13:12
16875.text: Expectation postponed is making the heart sick, but the thing desired is a tree of life when it does come.

16876.label: Proverbs 13:13
16876.text: He that has despised the word, from him a [debtor’s] pledge will be seized; but the one fearing the commandment is the one that will be rewarded.

16877.label: Proverbs 13:14
16877.text: The law of the wise one is a source of life, to turn one away from the snares of death.

16878.label: Proverbs 13:15
16878.text: Good insight itself gives favor, but the way of those dealing treacherously is rugged.

16879.label: Proverbs 13:16
16879.text: Everyone shrewd will act with knowledge, but the one that is stupid will spread abroad foolishness.

16880.label: Proverbs 13:17
16880.text: A messenger that is wicked will fall into bad, but a faithful envoy is a healing.

16881.label: Proverbs 13:18
16881.text: The one neglecting discipline [comes to] poverty and dishonor, but the one keeping a reproof is the one that is glorified.

16882.label: Proverbs 13:19
16882.text: Desire when realized is pleasurable to the soul; but it is something detestable to the stupid ones to turn away from bad.

16883.label: Proverbs 13:20
16883.text: He that is walking with wise persons will become wise, but he that is having dealings with the stupid ones will fare badly.

16884.label: Proverbs 13:21
16884.text: Sinners are the ones whom calamity pursues, but the righteous are the ones whom good rewards.

16885.label: Proverbs 13:22
16885.text: One who is good will leave an inheritance to sons of sons, and the wealth of the sinner is something treasured up for the righteous one.

16886.label: Proverbs 13:23
16886.text: Plowed ground of persons of little means [yields] a great deal of food, but there exists the one that is swept away for lack of judgment.

16887.label: Proverbs 13:24
16887.text: The one holding back his rod is hating his son, but the one loving him is he that does look for him with discipline.

16888.label: Proverbs 13:25
16888.text: The righteous is eating to the satisfaction of his soul, but the belly of the wicked ones will be empty.

16889.label: Proverbs 14:1
16889.text: The truly wise woman has built up her house, but the foolish one tears it down with her own hands.

16890.label: Proverbs 14:2
16890.text: The one walking in his uprightness is fearing Jehovah, but the one crooked in his ways is despising Him.

16891.label: Proverbs 14:3
16891.text: The rod of haughtiness is in the mouth of the foolish one, but the very lips of the wise ones will guard them.

16892.label: Proverbs 14:4
16892.text: Where there are no cattle the manger is clean, but the crop is abundant because of the power of a bull.

16893.label: Proverbs 14:5
16893.text: A faithful witness is one that will not lie, but a false witness launches forth mere lies.

16894.label: Proverbs 14:6
16894.text: The ridiculer has sought to find wisdom, and there is none; but to the understanding one knowledge is an easy thing.

16895.label: Proverbs 14:7
16895.text: Go away from in front of the stupid man, for you will certainly not take note of the lips of knowledge.

16896.label: Proverbs 14:8
16896.text: The wisdom of the shrewd is to understand his way, but the foolishness of stupid ones is deception.

16897.label: Proverbs 14:9
16897.text: Foolish are those who make a derision of guilt, but among the upright ones there is agreement.

16898.label: Proverbs 14:10
16898.text: The heart is aware of the bitterness of one’s soul, and with its rejoicing no stranger will intermeddle.

16899.label: Proverbs 14:11
16899.text: The house of wicked people will be annihilated, but the tent of the upright ones will flourish.

16900.label: Proverbs 14:12
16900.text: There exists a way that is upright before a man, but the ways of death are the end of it afterward.

16901.label: Proverbs 14:13
16901.text: Even in laughter the heart may be in pain; and grief is what rejoicing ends up in.

16902.label: Proverbs 14:14
16902.text: The one faithless at heart will be satisfied with the results of his own ways, but the good man with the results of his dealings.

16903.label: Proverbs 14:15
16903.text: Anyone inexperienced puts faith in every word, but the shrewd one considers his steps.

16904.label: Proverbs 14:16
16904.text: The wise one fears and is turning away from badness, but the stupid is becoming furious and self-confident.

16905.label: Proverbs 14:17
16905.text: He that is quick to anger will commit foolishness, but the man of thinking abilities is hated.

16906.label: Proverbs 14:18
16906.text: The inexperienced ones will certainly take possession of foolishness, but the shrewd ones will bear knowledge as a headdress.

16907.label: Proverbs 14:19
16907.text: Bad people will have to bow down before the good ones, and the wicked people at the gates of the righteous one.

16908.label: Proverbs 14:20
16908.text: Even to his fellowman one who is of little means is an object of hatred, but many are the friends of the rich person.

16909.label: Proverbs 14:21
16909.text: The one despising his own fellowman is sinning, but happy is he who is showing favor to the afflicted ones.

16910.label: Proverbs 14:22
16910.text: Will not those devising mischief go wandering about? But there are loving-kindness and trueness as regards those devising good.

16911.label: Proverbs 14:23
16911.text: By every kind of toil there comes to be an advantage, but merely the word of the lips [tends] to want.

16912.label: Proverbs 14:24
16912.text: The crown of the wise is their riches; the foolishness of the stupid ones is foolishness.

16913.label: Proverbs 14:25
16913.text: A true witness is delivering souls, but a deceitful one launches forth mere lies.

16914.label: Proverbs 14:26
16914.text: In the fear of Jehovah there is strong confidence, and for his sons there will come to be a refuge.

16915.label: Proverbs 14:27
16915.text: The fear of Jehovah is a well of life, to turn away from the snares of death.

16916.label: Proverbs 14:28
16916.text: In the multitude of people there is an adornment of a king, but in the lack of population is the ruin of a high official.

16917.label: Proverbs 14:29
16917.text: He that is slow to anger is abundant in discernment, but one that is impatient is exalting foolishness.

16918.label: Proverbs 14:30
16918.text: A calm heart is the life of the fleshly organism, but jealousy is rottenness to the bones.

16919.label: Proverbs 14:31
16919.text: He that is defrauding the lowly one has reproached his Maker, but the one showing favor to the poor one is glorifying Him.

16920.label: Proverbs 14:32
16920.text: Because of his badness the wicked will be pushed down, but the righteous will be finding refuge in his integrity.

16921.label: Proverbs 14:33
16921.text: In the heart of the understanding one there rests wisdom, and in the midst of stupid ones it becomes known.

16922.label: Proverbs 14:34
16922.text: Righteousness is what exalts a nation, but sin is something disgraceful to national groups.

16923.label: Proverbs 14:35
16923.text: The pleasure of a king is in the servant who is acting with insight, but his fury comes to be toward one acting shamefully.

16924.label: Proverbs 15:1
16924.text: An answer, when mild, turns away rage, but a word causing pain makes anger to come up.

16925.label: Proverbs 15:2
16925.text: The tongue of wise ones does good with knowledge, but the mouth of the stupid ones bubbles forth with foolishness.

16926.label: Proverbs 15:3
16926.text: The eyes of Jehovah are in every place, keeping watch upon the bad ones and the good ones.

16927.label: Proverbs 15:4
16927.text: The calmness of the tongue is a tree of life, but distortion in it means a breaking down in the spirit.

16928.label: Proverbs 15:5
16928.text: Anyone foolish disrespects the discipline of his father, but anyone regarding reproof is shrewd.

16929.label: Proverbs 15:6
16929.text: In the house of the righteous one there is an abundant store, but in the produce of the wicked one there is a becoming ostracized.

16930.label: Proverbs 15:7
16930.text: The lips of the wise ones keep scattering knowledge about, but the heart of the stupid ones is not like that.

16931.label: Proverbs 15:8
16931.text: The sacrifice of the wicked ones is something detestable to Jehovah, but the prayer of the upright ones is a pleasure to him.

16932.label: Proverbs 15:9
16932.text: The way of the wicked one is something detestable to Jehovah, but the one pursuing righteousness he loves.

16933.label: Proverbs 15:10
16933.text: Discipline is bad to the one leaving the path; anyone hating reproof will die.

16934.label: Proverbs 15:11
16934.text: Sheʹol and [the place of] destruction are in front of Jehovah. How much more so the hearts of the sons of mankind!

16935.label: Proverbs 15:12
16935.text: The ridiculer does not love the one reproving him. To the wise ones he will not go.

16936.label: Proverbs 15:13
16936.text: A joyful heart has a good effect on the countenance, but because of the pain of the heart there is a stricken spirit.

16937.label: Proverbs 15:14
16937.text: The understanding heart is one that searches for knowledge, but the mouth of stupid people is one that aspires to foolishness.

16938.label: Proverbs 15:15
16938.text: All the days of the afflicted one are bad; but the one that is good at heart [has] a feast constantly.

16939.label: Proverbs 15:16
16939.text: Better is a little in the fear of Jehovah than an abundant supply and confusion along with it.

16940.label: Proverbs 15:17
16940.text: Better is a dish of vegetables where there is love than a manger-fed bull and hatred along with it.

16941.label: Proverbs 15:18
16941.text: An enraged man stirs up contention, but one that is slow to anger quiets down quarreling.

16942.label: Proverbs 15:19
16942.text: The way of the lazy one is like a brier hedge, but the path of the upright ones is a way cast up.

16943.label: Proverbs 15:20
16943.text: A wise son is the one that makes a father rejoice, but a stupid man is despising his mother.

16944.label: Proverbs 15:21
16944.text: Foolishness is a rejoicing to one who is in want of heart, but the man of discernment is one who goes straight ahead.

16945.label: Proverbs 15:22
16945.text: There is a frustrating of plans where there is no confidential talk, but in the multitude of counselors there is accomplishment.

16946.label: Proverbs 15:23
16946.text: A man has rejoicing in the answer of his mouth, and a word at its right time is O how good!

16947.label: Proverbs 15:24
16947.text: The path of life is upward to one acting with insight, in order to turn away from Sheʹol down below.

16948.label: Proverbs 15:25
16948.text: The house of the self-exalted ones Jehovah will tear down, but he will fix the boundary of the widow.

16949.label: Proverbs 15:26
16949.text: The schemes of the bad one are something detestable to Jehovah, but pleasant sayings are clean.

16950.label: Proverbs 15:27
16950.text: The one making unjust profit is bringing ostracism upon his own house, but the hater of gifts is the one that will keep living.

16951.label: Proverbs 15:28
16951.text: The heart of the righteous one meditates so as to answer, but the mouth of the wicked ones bubbles forth with bad things.

16952.label: Proverbs 15:29
16952.text: Jehovah is far away from the wicked ones, but the prayer of the righteous ones he hears.

16953.label: Proverbs 15:30
16953.text: The brightness of the eyes makes the heart rejoice; a report that is good makes the bones fat.

16954.label: Proverbs 15:31
16954.text: The ear that is listening to the reproof of life lodges right in among wise people.

16955.label: Proverbs 15:32
16955.text: Anyone shunning discipline is rejecting his own soul, but the one listening to reproof is acquiring heart.

16956.label: Proverbs 15:33
16956.text: The fear of Jehovah is a discipline toward wisdom, and before glory there is humility.

16957.label: Proverbs 16:1
16957.text: To earthling man belong the arrangings of the heart, but from Jehovah is the answer of the tongue.

16958.label: Proverbs 16:2
16958.text: All the ways of a man are pure in his own eyes, but Jehovah is making an estimate of spirits.

16959.label: Proverbs 16:3
16959.text: Roll your works upon Jehovah himself and your plans will be firmly established.

16960.label: Proverbs 16:4
16960.text: Everything Jehovah has made for his purpose, yes, even the wicked one for the evil day.

16961.label: Proverbs 16:5
16961.text: Everyone that is proud in heart is something detestable to Jehovah. Hand [may join] to hand, [yet] one will not be free from punishment.

16962.label: Proverbs 16:6
16962.text: By loving-kindness and trueness error is atoned for, and in the fear of Jehovah one turns away from bad.

16963.label: Proverbs 16:7
16963.text: When Jehovah takes pleasure in the ways of a man he causes even his enemies themselves to be at peace with him.

16964.label: Proverbs 16:8
16964.text: Better is a little with righteousness than an abundance of products without justice.

16965.label: Proverbs 16:9
16965.text: The heart of earthling man may think out his way, but Jehovah himself does the directing of his steps.

16966.label: Proverbs 16:10
16966.text: Inspired decision should be upon the lips of a king; in judgment his mouth should not prove unfaithful.

16967.label: Proverbs 16:11
16967.text: The just indicator and scales belong to Jehovah; all the stone weights of the bag are his work.

16968.label: Proverbs 16:12
16968.text: The doing of wickedness is something detestable to kings, for by righteousness is the throne firmly established.

16969.label: Proverbs 16:13
16969.text: The lips of righteousness are a pleasure to a grand king; and the speaker of upright things he loves.

16970.label: Proverbs 16:14
16970.text: The rage of a king means messengers of death, but the wise man is one that averts it.

16971.label: Proverbs 16:15
16971.text: In the light of the king’s face there is life, and his goodwill is like the cloud of spring rain.

16972.label: Proverbs 16:16
16972.text: The getting of wisdom is O how much better than gold! And the getting of understanding is to be chosen more than silver.

16973.label: Proverbs 16:17
16973.text: The highway of the upright ones is to turn away from bad. One who is safeguarding his way is keeping his soul.

16974.label: Proverbs 16:18
16974.text: Pride is before a crash, and a haughty spirit before stumbling.

16975.label: Proverbs 16:19
16975.text: Better is it to be lowly in spirit with the meek ones than to divide spoil with the self-exalted ones.

16976.label: Proverbs 16:20
16976.text: He that is showing insight in a matter will find good, and happy is he that is trusting in Jehovah.

16977.label: Proverbs 16:21
16977.text: The one that is wise in heart will be called understanding, and he that is sweet in [his] lips adds persuasiveness.

16978.label: Proverbs 16:22
16978.text: To its owners insight is a well of life; and the discipline of the foolish ones is foolishness.

16979.label: Proverbs 16:23
16979.text: The heart of the wise one causes his mouth to show insight, and to his lips it adds persuasiveness.

16980.label: Proverbs 16:24
16980.text: Pleasant sayings are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and a healing to the bones.

16981.label: Proverbs 16:25
16981.text: There exists a way that is upright before a man, but the ways of death are the end of it afterward.

16982.label: Proverbs 16:26
16982.text: The soul of the hard worker has worked hard for him, because his mouth has pressed him hard.

16983.label: Proverbs 16:27
16983.text: A good-for-nothing man is digging up what is bad, and upon his lips there is, as it were, a scorching fire.

16984.label: Proverbs 16:28
16984.text: A man of intrigues keeps sending forth contention, and a slanderer is separating those familiar with one another.

16985.label: Proverbs 16:29
16985.text: A man of violence will seduce his fellow, and certainly causes him to go in a way that is not good.

16986.label: Proverbs 16:30
16986.text: He is blinking with his eyes to scheme up intrigues. Pinching his lips together, he certainly brings mischief to completion.

16987.label: Proverbs 16:31
16987.text: Gray-headedness is a crown of beauty when it is found in the way of righteousness.

16988.label: Proverbs 16:32
16988.text: He that is slow to anger is better than a mighty man, and he that is controlling his spirit than the one capturing a city.

16989.label: Proverbs 16:33
16989.text: Into the lap the lot is cast down, but every decision by it is from Jehovah.

16990.label: Proverbs 17:1
16990.text: Better is a dry piece of bread with which there is quietness than a house full of the sacrifices of quarreling.

16991.label: Proverbs 17:2
16991.text: A servant that is showing insight will rule over the son who is acting shamefully, and in among the brothers he will have a share of the inheritance.

16992.label: Proverbs 17:3
16992.text: The refining pot is for silver and the furnace for gold, but Jehovah is the examiner of hearts.

16993.label: Proverbs 17:4
16993.text: The evildoer is paying attention to the lip of hurtfulness. A falsifier is giving ear to the tongue causing adversities.

16994.label: Proverbs 17:5
16994.text: He that is holding the one of little means in derision has reproached his Maker. He that is joyful at [another’s] disaster will not be free from punishment.

16995.label: Proverbs 17:6
16995.text: The crown of old men is the grandsons, and the beauty of sons is their fathers.

16996.label: Proverbs 17:7
16996.text: For anyone senseless the lip of uprightness is not fitting. How much less so for a noble the lip of falsehood!

16997.label: Proverbs 17:8
16997.text: The gift is a stone winning favor in the eyes of its grand owner. Everywhere that he turns he has success.

16998.label: Proverbs 17:9
16998.text: The one covering over transgression is seeking love, and he that keeps talking about a matter is separating those familiar with one another.

16999.label: Proverbs 17:10
16999.text: A rebuke works deeper in one having understanding than striking a stupid one a hundred times.

17000.label: Proverbs 17:11
17000.text: Only rebellion is what the bad one keeps seeking, and cruel is the messenger that is sent against him.

17001.label: Proverbs 17:12
17001.text: Let there be an encountering by a man of a bear bereaved of its cubs rather than anyone stupid in his foolishness.

17002.label: Proverbs 17:13
17002.text: As for anyone repaying bad for good, bad will not move away from his house.

17003.label: Proverbs 17:14
17003.text: The beginning of contention is as one letting out waters; so before the quarrel has burst forth, take your leave.

17004.label: Proverbs 17:15
17004.text: Anyone pronouncing the wicked one righteous and anyone pronouncing the righteous one wicked —even both of them are something detestable to Jehovah.

17005.label: Proverbs 17:16
17005.text: Why is it that there is in the hand of a stupid one the price to acquire wisdom, when he has no heart?

17006.label: Proverbs 17:17
17006.text: A true companion is loving all the time, and is a brother that is born for when there is distress.

17007.label: Proverbs 17:18
17007.text: A man that is wanting in heart shakes hands, going full surety before his companion.

17008.label: Proverbs 17:19
17008.text: Anyone loving transgression is loving a struggle. Anyone making his entryway high is seeking a crash.

17009.label: Proverbs 17:20
17009.text: He that is crooked at heart will not find good, and he that is turned around in his tongue will fall into calamity.

17010.label: Proverbs 17:21
17010.text: Anyone becoming father to a stupid child—it is a grief to him; and the father of a senseless child does not rejoice.

17011.label: Proverbs 17:22
17011.text: A heart that is joyful does good as a curer, but a spirit that is stricken makes the bones dry.

17012.label: Proverbs 17:23
17012.text: One who is wicked will take even a bribe from the bosom to bend the paths of judgment.

17013.label: Proverbs 17:24
17013.text: Wisdom is before the face of the understanding one, but the eyes of the stupid one are at the extremity of the earth.

17014.label: Proverbs 17:25
17014.text: A stupid son is a vexation to his father and a bitterness to her that gave him birth.

17015.label: Proverbs 17:26
17015.text: Furthermore, the laying of a fine upon the righteous one is not good. To strike nobles is against what is upright.

17016.label: Proverbs 17:27
17016.text: Anyone holding back his sayings is possessed of knowledge, and a man of discernment is cool of spirit.

17017.label: Proverbs 17:28
17017.text: Even anyone foolish, when keeping silent, will be regarded as wise; anyone closing up his own lips, as having understanding.

17018.label: Proverbs 18:1
17018.text: One isolating himself will seek [his own] selfish longing; against all practical wisdom he will break forth.

17019.label: Proverbs 18:2
17019.text: Anyone stupid finds no delight in discernment, except that his heart should uncover itself.

17020.label: Proverbs 18:3
17020.text: When a wicked one comes in, contempt also must come in; and along with dishonor there is reproach.

17021.label: Proverbs 18:4
17021.text: The words of a man’s mouth are deep waters. The well of wisdom is a torrent bubbling forth.

17022.label: Proverbs 18:5
17022.text: The showing of partiality to the wicked one is not good, nor the turning aside of the righteous one in judgment.

17023.label: Proverbs 18:6
17023.text: The lips of one who is stupid enter into quarreling, and his very mouth calls even for strokes.

17024.label: Proverbs 18:7
17024.text: The mouth of the stupid one is the ruin of him, and his lips are a snare for his soul.

17025.label: Proverbs 18:8
17025.text: The words of the slanderer are like things to be swallowed greedily, which do go down into the innermost parts of the belly.

17026.label: Proverbs 18:9
17026.text: Also, the one showing himself slack in his work —he is a brother to the one causing ruin.

17027.label: Proverbs 18:10
17027.text: The name of Jehovah is a strong tower. Into it the righteous runs and is given protection.

17028.label: Proverbs 18:11
17028.text: The valuable things of the rich are his strong town, and they are like a protective wall in his imagination.

17029.label: Proverbs 18:12
17029.text: Before a crash the heart of a man is lofty, and before glory there is humility.

17030.label: Proverbs 18:13
17030.text: When anyone is replying to a matter before he hears [it], that is foolishness on his part and a humiliation.

17031.label: Proverbs 18:14
17031.text: The spirit of a man can put up with his malady; but as for a stricken spirit, who can bear it?

17032.label: Proverbs 18:15
17032.text: The heart of the understanding one acquires knowledge, and the ear of wise ones seeks to find knowledge.

17033.label: Proverbs 18:16
17033.text: A man’s gift will make a large opening for him, and it will lead him even before great people.

17034.label: Proverbs 18:17
17034.text: The one first in his legal case is righteous; his fellow comes in and certainly searches him through.

17035.label: Proverbs 18:18
17035.text: The lot puts even contentions to rest, and it separates even the mighty from one another.

17036.label: Proverbs 18:19
17036.text: A brother who is transgressed against is more than a strong town; and there are contentions that are like the bar of a dwelling tower.

17037.label: Proverbs 18:20
17037.text: From the fruitage of a man’s mouth his belly will be satisfied; he will be satisfied even with the produce of his lips.

17038.label: Proverbs 18:21
17038.text: Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and he that is loving it will eat its fruitage.

17039.label: Proverbs 18:22
17039.text: Has one found a [good] wife? One has found a good thing, and one gets goodwill from Jehovah.

17040.label: Proverbs 18:23
17040.text: Entreaties the one of little means speaks out, but one that is rich answers in a strong way.

17041.label: Proverbs 18:24
17041.text: There exist companions disposed to break one another to pieces, but there exists a friend sticking closer than a brother.

17042.label: Proverbs 19:1
17042.text: Anyone of little means who is walking in his integrity is better than the one crooked in his lips, and the one that is stupid.

17043.label: Proverbs 19:2
17043.text: Also, that the soul should be without knowledge is not good, and he that is hastening with his feet is sinning.

17044.label: Proverbs 19:3
17044.text: It is the foolishness of an earthling man that distorts his way, and so his heart becomes enraged against Jehovah himself.

17045.label: Proverbs 19:4
17045.text: Wealth is what adds many companions, but one that is lowly gets separated even from his companion.

17046.label: Proverbs 19:5
17046.text: A false witness will not be free from punishment, and he that launches forth lies will not escape.

17047.label: Proverbs 19:6
17047.text: Many are those who soften the face of a noble, and everybody is a companion to the man making gifts.

17048.label: Proverbs 19:7
17048.text: The brothers of one of little means have all hated him. How much farther have his personal friends kept away from him! He is pursuing with things to say; they are not.

17049.label: Proverbs 19:8
17049.text: He that is acquiring heart is loving his own soul. He that is guarding discernment is going to find good.

17050.label: Proverbs 19:9
17050.text: The false witness will not be free from punishment, and he that launches forth lies will perish.

17051.label: Proverbs 19:10
17051.text: Luxury is not fitting for anyone stupid. How much less for a servant to rule over princes!

17052.label: Proverbs 19:11
17052.text: The insight of a man certainly slows down his anger, and it is beauty on his part to pass over transgression.

17053.label: Proverbs 19:12
17053.text: The raging of a king is a growling like that of a maned young lion, but his goodwill is like the dew upon the vegetation.

17054.label: Proverbs 19:13
17054.text: A stupid son means adversities to his father, and the contentions of a wife are as a leaking roof that drives one away.

17055.label: Proverbs 19:14
17055.text: The inheritance from fathers is a house and wealth, but a discreet wife is from Jehovah.

17056.label: Proverbs 19:15
17056.text: Laziness causes a deep sleep to fall, and a slack soul goes hungry.

17057.label: Proverbs 19:16
17057.text: He that is keeping the commandment is keeping his soul; he that is despising his ways will be put to death.

17058.label: Proverbs 19:17
17058.text: He that is showing favor to the lowly one is lending to Jehovah, and his treatment He will repay to him.

17059.label: Proverbs 19:18
17059.text: Chastise your son while there exists hope; and to the putting of him to death do not lift up your soul[ful desire].

17060.label: Proverbs 19:19
17060.text: He that is of great rage will be bearing the fine; for if you would deliver [him], you will also keep doing it again and again.

17061.label: Proverbs 19:20
17061.text: Listen to counsel and accept discipline, in order that you may become wise in your future.

17062.label: Proverbs 19:21
17062.text: Many are the plans in the heart of a man, but the counsel of Jehovah is what will stand.

17063.label: Proverbs 19:22
17063.text: The desirable thing in earthling man is his loving-kindness; and one of little means is better than a lying man.

17064.label: Proverbs 19:23
17064.text: The fear of Jehovah tends toward life, and one will spend the night satisfied; one will not be visited with what is bad.

17065.label: Proverbs 19:24
17065.text: The lazy one has hidden his hand in the banquet bowl; he cannot bring it back even to his own mouth.

17066.label: Proverbs 19:25
17066.text: The ridiculer you should strike, that the inexperienced one may become shrewd; and there should be a reproving of the understanding one, that he may discern knowledge.

17067.label: Proverbs 19:26
17067.text: He that is maltreating a father [and] that chases a mother away is a son acting shamefully and disgracefully.

17068.label: Proverbs 19:27
17068.text: Cease, my son, to listen to discipline [and it will mean] to stray from the sayings of knowledge.

17069.label: Proverbs 19:28
17069.text: A good-for-nothing witness derides justice, and the very mouth of wicked people swallows down what is hurtful.

17070.label: Proverbs 19:29
17070.text: Judgments have been firmly established for ridiculers, and strokes for the back of stupid ones.

17071.label: Proverbs 20:1
17071.text: Wine is a ridiculer, intoxicating liquor is boisterous, and everyone going astray by it is not wise.

17072.label: Proverbs 20:2
17072.text: The frightfulness of a king is a growling like that of a maned young lion. Anyone drawing his fury against himself is sinning against his own soul.

17073.label: Proverbs 20:3
17073.text: It is a glory for a man to desist from disputing, but everyone foolish will burst out [in it].

17074.label: Proverbs 20:4
17074.text: Because of winter the lazy one will not plow; he will be begging in reaping time, but there will be nothing.

17075.label: Proverbs 20:5
