17075.text: Counsel in the heart of a man is as deep waters, but the man of discernment is one that will draw it up.

17076.label: Proverbs 20:6
17076.text: A multitude of men will proclaim each one his own loving-kindness, but a faithful man who can find?

17077.label: Proverbs 20:7
17077.text: The righteous is walking in his integrity. Happy are his sons after him.

17078.label: Proverbs 20:8
17078.text: The king is sitting upon the throne of judgment, scattering all badness with his own eyes.

17079.label: Proverbs 20:9
17079.text: Who can say: “I have cleansed my heart; I have become pure from my sin”?

17080.label: Proverbs 20:10
17080.text: Two sorts of weights and two sorts of eʹphah measures —they are both of them together something detestable to Jehovah.

17081.label: Proverbs 20:11
17081.text: Even by his practices a boy makes himself recognized as to whether his activity is pure and upright.

17082.label: Proverbs 20:12
17082.text: The hearing ear and the seeing eye—Jehovah himself has made even both of them.

17083.label: Proverbs 20:13
17083.text: Do not love sleep, that you may not come to poverty. Open your eyes; be satisfied with bread.

17084.label: Proverbs 20:14
17084.text: “It is bad, bad!” says the buyer, and he is going his way. Then it is that he boasts about himself.

17085.label: Proverbs 20:15
17085.text: There exists gold, also an abundance of corals; but the lips of knowledge are precious vessels.

17086.label: Proverbs 20:16
17086.text: Take one’s garment, in case one has gone surety for a stranger; and in the instance of a foreign woman, seize from him a pledge.

17087.label: Proverbs 20:17
17087.text: Bread [gained by] falsehood is pleasurable to a man, but afterward his mouth will be filled with gravel.

17088.label: Proverbs 20:18
17088.text: By counsel plans themselves are firmly established, and by skillful direction carry on your war.

17089.label: Proverbs 20:19
17089.text: He that is going about as a slanderer is uncovering confidential talk; and with one that is enticed with his lips you must have no fellowship.

17090.label: Proverbs 20:20
17090.text: As for anyone calling down evil upon his father and his mother, his lamp will be extinguished at the approach of darkness.

17091.label: Proverbs 20:21
17091.text: An inheritance is being got by greed at first, but its own future will not be blessed.

17092.label: Proverbs 20:22
17092.text: Do not say: “I will pay back evil!” Hope in Jehovah, and he will save you.

17093.label: Proverbs 20:23
17093.text: Two sorts of weights are something detestable to Jehovah, and a cheating pair of scales is not good.

17094.label: Proverbs 20:24
17094.text: From Jehovah are the steppings of an able-bodied man. As regards earthling man, how can he discern his way?

17095.label: Proverbs 20:25
17095.text: It is a snare when earthling man has rashly cried out, “Holy!” and after vows [he is disposed] to make examination.

17096.label: Proverbs 20:26
17096.text: A wise king is scattering wicked people, and he turns around upon them a wheel.

17097.label: Proverbs 20:27
17097.text: The breath of earthling man is the lamp of Jehovah, carefully searching all the innermost parts of the belly.

17098.label: Proverbs 20:28
17098.text: Loving-kindness and trueness —they safeguard the king; and by loving-kindness he has sustained his throne.

17099.label: Proverbs 20:29
17099.text: The beauty of young men is their power, and the splendor of old men is their gray-headedness.

17100.label: Proverbs 20:30
17100.text: Bruising wounds are what scours away the bad; and strokes, the innermost parts of the belly.

17101.label: Proverbs 21:1
17101.text: A king’s heart is as streams of water in the hand of Jehovah. Everywhere that he delights to, he turns it.

17102.label: Proverbs 21:2
17102.text: Every way of a man is upright in his own eyes, but Jehovah is making an estimate of hearts.

17103.label: Proverbs 21:3
17103.text: To carry on righteousness and judgment is more preferable to Jehovah than sacrifice.

17104.label: Proverbs 21:4
17104.text: Haughty eyes and an arrogant heart, the lamp of the wicked ones, are sin.

17105.label: Proverbs 21:5
17105.text: The plans of the diligent one surely make for advantage, but everyone that is hasty surely heads for want.

17106.label: Proverbs 21:6
17106.text: The getting of treasures by a false tongue is an exhalation driven away, in the case of those seeking death.

17107.label: Proverbs 21:7
17107.text: The very despoiling by the wicked ones will drag them away, for they have refused to do justice.

17108.label: Proverbs 21:8
17108.text: A man, even a stranger, is crooked in [his] way; but the pure one is upright in his activity.

17109.label: Proverbs 21:9
17109.text: Better is it to dwell upon a corner of a roof than with a contentious wife, although in a house in common.

17110.label: Proverbs 21:10
17110.text: The very soul of the wicked one has craved what is bad; his fellow will be shown no favor in his eyes.

17111.label: Proverbs 21:11
17111.text: By the laying of a fine on the ridiculer the inexperienced becomes wise; and by one’s giving insight to a wise person he gets knowledge.

17112.label: Proverbs 21:12
17112.text: The Righteous One is giving consideration to the house of the wicked one, subverting the wicked ones to [their] calamity.

17113.label: Proverbs 21:13
17113.text: As for anyone stopping up his ear from the complaining cry of the lowly one, he himself also will call and not be answered.

17114.label: Proverbs 21:14
17114.text: A gift made in secrecy subdues anger; and a bribe in the bosom, strong rage.

17115.label: Proverbs 21:15
17115.text: It is a rejoicing for the righteous one to do justice, but there is something terrible for those practicing what is hurtful.

17116.label: Proverbs 21:16
17116.text: As for a man wandering from the way of insight, he will rest in the very congregation of those impotent in death.

17117.label: Proverbs 21:17
17117.text: He that is loving merriment will be an individual in want; he that is loving wine and oil will not gain riches.

17118.label: Proverbs 21:18
17118.text: The wicked is a ransom for the righteous one; and the one dealing treacherously takes the place of the upright ones.

17119.label: Proverbs 21:19
17119.text: Better is it to dwell in a wilderness land than with a contentious wife along with vexation.

17120.label: Proverbs 21:20
17120.text: Desirable treasure and oil are in the abode of the wise one, but the man that is stupid will swallow it up.

17121.label: Proverbs 21:21
17121.text: He that is pursuing righteousness and loving-kindness will find life, righteousness and glory.

17122.label: Proverbs 21:22
17122.text: A wise one has scaled even the city of mighty men, that he might bring down the strength of its confidence.

17123.label: Proverbs 21:23
17123.text: He that is keeping his mouth and his tongue is keeping his soul from distresses.

17124.label: Proverbs 21:24
17124.text: Presumptuous, self-assuming braggart is the name of the one who is acting in a fury of presumptuousness.

17125.label: Proverbs 21:25
17125.text: The very craving of the lazy will put him to death, for his hands have refused to work.

17126.label: Proverbs 21:26
17126.text: All the day he has shown himself eagerly craving, but the righteous one gives and holds nothing back.

17127.label: Proverbs 21:27
17127.text: The sacrifice of the wicked ones is something detestable. How much more so when one brings it along with loose conduct.

17128.label: Proverbs 21:28
17128.text: A lying witness will perish, but the man that is listening will speak even forever.

17129.label: Proverbs 21:29
17129.text: A wicked man has put on a bold face, but the upright is the one that will firmly establish his ways.

17130.label: Proverbs 21:30
17130.text: There is no wisdom, nor any discernment, nor any counsel in opposition to Jehovah.

17131.label: Proverbs 21:31
17131.text: The horse is something prepared for the day of battle, but salvation belongs to Jehovah.

17132.label: Proverbs 22:1
17132.text: A name is to be chosen rather than abundant riches; favor is better than even silver and gold.

17133.label: Proverbs 22:2
17133.text: The rich one and the one of little means have met each other. The Maker of them all is Jehovah.

17134.label: Proverbs 22:3
17134.text: Shrewd is the one that has seen the calamity and proceeds to conceal himself, but the inexperienced have passed along and must suffer the penalty.

17135.label: Proverbs 22:4
17135.text: The result of humility [and] the fear of Jehovah is riches and glory and life.

17136.label: Proverbs 22:5
17136.text: Thorns [and] traps are in the way of the crooked one; he that is guarding his soul keeps far away from them.

17137.label: Proverbs 22:6
17137.text: Train up a boy according to the way for him; even when he grows old he will not turn aside from it.

17138.label: Proverbs 22:7
17138.text: The rich is the one that rules over those of little means, and the borrower is servant to the man doing the lending.

17139.label: Proverbs 22:8
17139.text: He that is sowing unrighteousness will reap what is hurtful, but the very rod of his fury will come to its end.

17140.label: Proverbs 22:9
17140.text: He that is kindly in eye will be blessed, for he has given of his food to the lowly one.

17141.label: Proverbs 22:10
17141.text: Drive away the ridiculer, that contention may go out and that legal contest and dishonor may cease.

17142.label: Proverbs 22:11
17142.text: The one loving purity of heart —for the charm of his lips the king will be his companion.

17143.label: Proverbs 22:12
17143.text: The eyes of Jehovah himself have safeguarded knowledge, but he subverts the words of the treacherous one.

17144.label: Proverbs 22:13
17144.text: The lazy one has said: “There is a lion outside! In the midst of the public squares I shall be murdered!”

17145.label: Proverbs 22:14
17145.text: The mouth of strange women is a deep pit. The one denounced by Jehovah will fall into it.

17146.label: Proverbs 22:15
17146.text: Foolishness is tied up with the heart of a boy; the rod of discipline is what will remove it far from him.

17147.label: Proverbs 22:16
17147.text: He that is defrauding the lowly one to supply many things to himself, he also that is giving to the rich one, is surely destined for want.

17148.label: Proverbs 22:17
17148.text: Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise ones, that you may apply your very heart to my knowledge.

17149.label: Proverbs 22:18
17149.text: For it is pleasant that you should keep them in your belly, that they may be firmly established together upon your lips.

17150.label: Proverbs 22:19
17150.text: For your confidence to come to be in Jehovah himself I have given you knowledge today, even you.

17151.label: Proverbs 22:20
17151.text: Have I not written you heretofore with counselings and knowledge,

17152.label: Proverbs 22:21
17152.text: to show you the truthfulness of true sayings, so as to return sayings that are the truth—to the one sending you forth?

17153.label: Proverbs 22:22
17153.text: Do not rob the lowly one because he is lowly, and do not crush the afflicted one in the gate.

17154.label: Proverbs 22:23
17154.text: For Jehovah himself will plead their cause, and he will certainly rob of soul those robbing them.

17155.label: Proverbs 22:24
17155.text: Do not have companionship with anyone given to anger; and with a man having fits of rage you must not enter in,

17156.label: Proverbs 22:25
17156.text: that you may not get familiar with his paths and certainly take a snare for your soul.

17157.label: Proverbs 22:26
17157.text: Do not get to be among those striking hands, among those who go security for loans.

17158.label: Proverbs 22:27
17158.text: If you have nothing to pay, why should he take your bed from under you?

17159.label: Proverbs 22:28
17159.text: Do not move back a boundary of long ago, which your forefathers have made.

17160.label: Proverbs 22:29
17160.text: Have you beheld a man skillful in his work? Before kings is where he will station himself; he will not station himself before commonplace men.

17161.label: Proverbs 23:1
17161.text: In case you should sit down to feed yourself with a king, you should diligently consider what is before you,

17162.label: Proverbs 23:2
17162.text: and you must put a knife to your throat if you are the owner of soul[ful desire].

17163.label: Proverbs 23:3
17163.text: Do not show yourself craving his tasty dishes, as it is the food of lies.

17164.label: Proverbs 23:4
17164.text: Do not toil to gain riches. Cease from your own understanding.

17165.label: Proverbs 23:5
17165.text: Have you caused your eyes to glance at it, when it is nothing? For without fail it makes wings for itself like those of an eagle and flies away toward the heavens.

17166.label: Proverbs 23:6
17166.text: Do not feed yourself with the food of anyone of ungenerous eye, nor show yourself craving his tasty dishes.

17167.label: Proverbs 23:7
17167.text: For as one that has calculated within his soul, so he is. “Eat and drink,” he says to you, but his heart itself is not with you.

17168.label: Proverbs 23:8
17168.text: Your morsel that you have eaten, you will vomit it out, and you will have wasted your pleasant words.

17169.label: Proverbs 23:9
17169.text: Into the ears of a stupid one do not speak, for he will despise your discreet words.

17170.label: Proverbs 23:10
17170.text: Do not move back the boundary of long ago, and into the field of fatherless boys do not enter.

17171.label: Proverbs 23:11
17171.text: For their Redeemer is strong; he himself will plead their cause with you.

17172.label: Proverbs 23:12
17172.text: Do bring your heart to discipline and your ear to the sayings of knowledge.

17173.label: Proverbs 23:13
17173.text: Do not hold back discipline from the mere boy. In case you beat him with the rod, he will not die.

17174.label: Proverbs 23:14
17174.text: With the rod you yourself should beat him, that you may deliver his very soul from Sheʹol itself.

17175.label: Proverbs 23:15
17175.text: My son, if your heart has become wise, my heart will rejoice, even mine.

17176.label: Proverbs 23:16
17176.text: And my kidneys will exult when your lips speak uprightness.

17177.label: Proverbs 23:17
17177.text: Let your heart not be envious of sinners, but be in the fear of Jehovah all day long.

17178.label: Proverbs 23:18
17178.text: For in that case there will exist a future, and your own hope will not be cut off.

17179.label: Proverbs 23:19
17179.text: You, O my son, hear and become wise, and lead your heart on in the way.

17180.label: Proverbs 23:20
17180.text: Do not come to be among heavy drinkers of wine, among those who are gluttonous eaters of flesh.

17181.label: Proverbs 23:21
17181.text: For a drunkard and a glutton will come to poverty, and drowsiness will clothe one with mere rags.

17182.label: Proverbs 23:22
17182.text: Listen to your father who caused your birth, and do not despise your mother just because she has grown old.

17183.label: Proverbs 23:23
17183.text: Buy truth itself and do not sell it—wisdom and discipline and understanding.

17184.label: Proverbs 23:24
17184.text: The father of a righteous one will without fail be joyful; the one becoming father to a wise one will also rejoice in him.

17185.label: Proverbs 23:25
17185.text: Your father and your mother will rejoice, and she that gave birth to you will be joyful.

17186.label: Proverbs 23:26
17186.text: My son, do give your heart to me, and may those eyes of yours take pleasure in my own ways.

17187.label: Proverbs 23:27
17187.text: For a prostitute is a deep pit and a foreign woman is a narrow well.

17188.label: Proverbs 23:28
17188.text: Surely she, just like a robber, lies in wait; and among men she increases the treacherous ones.

17189.label: Proverbs 23:29
17189.text: Who has woe? Who has uneasiness? Who has contentions? Who has concern? Who has wounds for no reason? Who has dullness of eyes?

17190.label: Proverbs 23:30
17190.text: Those staying a long time with the wine, those coming in to search out mixed wine.

17191.label: Proverbs 23:31
17191.text: Do not look at wine when it exhibits a red color, when it gives off its sparkle in the cup, [when] it goes with a slickness.

17192.label: Proverbs 23:32
17192.text: At its end it bites just like a serpent, and it secretes poison just like a viper.

17193.label: Proverbs 23:33
17193.text: Your own eyes will see strange things, and your own heart will speak perverse things.

17194.label: Proverbs 23:34
17194.text: And you will certainly become like one lying down in the heart of the sea, even like one lying down at the top of a mast.

17195.label: Proverbs 23:35
17195.text: “They have struck me, but I did not become sick; they have smitten me, but I did not know it. When shall I wake up? I shall seek it yet some more.”

17196.label: Proverbs 24:1
17196.text: Do not be envious of bad men, and do not show yourself craving to get in with them.

17197.label: Proverbs 24:2
17197.text: For despoiling is what their heart keeps meditating, and trouble is what their own lips keep speaking.

17198.label: Proverbs 24:3
17198.text: By wisdom a household will be built up, and by discernment it will prove firmly established.

17199.label: Proverbs 24:4
17199.text: And by knowledge will the interior rooms be filled with all precious and pleasant things of value.

17200.label: Proverbs 24:5
17200.text: One wise in strength is an able-bodied man, and a man of knowledge is reinforcing power.

17201.label: Proverbs 24:6
17201.text: For by skillful direction you will carry on your war, and in the multitude of counselors there is salvation.

17202.label: Proverbs 24:7
17202.text: For a foolish one true wisdom is too high; in the gate he will not open his mouth.

17203.label: Proverbs 24:8
17203.text: As for anyone scheming to do bad, he will be called a mere master at evil ideas.

17204.label: Proverbs 24:9
17204.text: The loose conduct of foolishness is sin, and a ridiculer is something detestable to mankind.

17205.label: Proverbs 24:10
17205.text: Have you shown yourself discouraged in the day of distress? Your power will be scanty.

17206.label: Proverbs 24:11
17206.text: Deliver those who are being taken away to death; and those staggering to the slaughter, O may you hold [them] back.

17207.label: Proverbs 24:12
17207.text: In case you should say: “Look! We did not know of this,” will not he himself that is making an estimate of hearts discern it, and he himself that is observing your soul know and certainly pay back to earthling man according to his activity?

17208.label: Proverbs 24:13
17208.text: My son, eat honey, for it is good; and let sweet comb honey be upon your palate.

17209.label: Proverbs 24:14
17209.text: In the same way, do know wisdom for your soul. If you have found [it], then there exists a future, and your own hope will not be cut off.

17210.label: Proverbs 24:15
17210.text: Do not, as a wicked one, lie in wait for the abiding place of the righteous one; do not despoil his resting-place.

17211.label: Proverbs 24:16
17211.text: For the righteous one may fall even seven times, and he will certainly get up; but the wicked ones will be made to stumble by calamity.

17212.label: Proverbs 24:17
17212.text: When your enemy falls, do not rejoice; and when he is caused to stumble, may your heart not be joyful,

17213.label: Proverbs 24:18
17213.text: that Jehovah may not see and it be bad in his eyes and he certainly turn back his anger from against him.

17214.label: Proverbs 24:19
17214.text: Do not show yourself heated up at evildoers. Do not become envious of wicked people.

17215.label: Proverbs 24:20
17215.text: For there will prove to be no future for anyone bad; the very lamp of wicked people will be extinguished.

17216.label: Proverbs 24:21
17216.text: My son, fear Jehovah and the king. With those who are for a change, do not intermeddle.

17217.label: Proverbs 24:22
17217.text: For their disaster will arise so suddenly, that who is aware of the extinction of those who are for a change?

17218.label: Proverbs 24:23
17218.text: These [sayings] also are for the wise ones: The showing of partiality in judgment is not good.

17219.label: Proverbs 24:24
17219.text: He that is saying to the wicked one: “You are righteous,” the peoples will execrate him, national groups will denounce him.

17220.label: Proverbs 24:25
17220.text: But for those reproving [him] it will be pleasant, and upon them there will come the blessing of good.

17221.label: Proverbs 24:26
17221.text: Lips will he kiss who is replying in a straightforward way.

17222.label: Proverbs 24:27
17222.text: Prepare your work out of doors, and make it ready for yourself in the field. Afterward you must also build up your household.

17223.label: Proverbs 24:28
17223.text: Do not become a witness against your fellowman without grounds. Then you would have to be foolish with your lips.

17224.label: Proverbs 24:29
17224.text: Do not say: “Just as he did to me, so I am going to do to him. I shall repay to each one according to his acting.”

17225.label: Proverbs 24:30
17225.text: I passed along by the field of the lazy individual and by the vineyard of the man in need of heart.

17226.label: Proverbs 24:31
17226.text: And, look! all of it produced weeds. Nettles covered its very surface, and its stone wall itself had been torn down.

17227.label: Proverbs 24:32
17227.text: So I proceeded to behold, I myself; I began taking [it] to heart; I saw, I took the discipline:

17228.label: Proverbs 24:33
17228.text: A little sleeping, a little slumbering, a little folding of the hands to lie down,

17229.label: Proverbs 24:34
17229.text: and as a highwayman your poverty will certainly come and your neediness as an armed man.

17230.label: Proverbs 25:1
17230.text: These also are the proverbs of Solʹo·mon that the men of Hez·e·kiʹah the king of Judah transcribed:

17231.label: Proverbs 25:2
17231.text: The glory of God is the keeping of a matter secret, and the glory of kings is the searching through a matter.

17232.label: Proverbs 25:3
17232.text: The heavens for height and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings, that is unsearchable.

17233.label: Proverbs 25:4
17233.text: Let there be a removing of scummy dross from the silver, and all of it will come forth refined.

17234.label: Proverbs 25:5
17234.text: Let there be the removing of the wicked one before the king, and his throne will be firmly established by righteousness itself.

17235.label: Proverbs 25:6
17235.text: Do not do yourself honor before the king, and in the place of great ones do not stand.

17236.label: Proverbs 25:7
17236.text: For it is better [for him] to say to you: “Come up here,” than to abase you before a noble whom your eyes have seen.

17237.label: Proverbs 25:8
17237.text: Do not go forth to conduct a legal case hastily, that it may not be a question of what you will do in the culmination of it when your fellowman now humiliates you.

17238.label: Proverbs 25:9
17238.text: Plead your own cause with your fellowman, and do not reveal the confidential talk of another;

17239.label: Proverbs 25:10
17239.text: that the one listening may not put you to shame and the bad report by you can have no recall.

17240.label: Proverbs 25:11
17240.text: As apples of gold in silver carvings is a word spoken at the right time for it.

17241.label: Proverbs 25:12
17241.text: An earring of gold, and an ornament of special gold, is a wise reprover upon the hearing ear.

17242.label: Proverbs 25:13
17242.text: Just like the coolness of snow in the day of harvest is the faithful envoy to those sending him, for he restores the very soul of his masters.

17243.label: Proverbs 25:14
17243.text: As vaporous clouds and a wind without any downpour is a man boasting himself about a gift in falsehood.

17244.label: Proverbs 25:15
17244.text: By patience a commander is induced, and a mild tongue itself can break a bone.

17245.label: Proverbs 25:16
17245.text: Is it honey that you have found? Eat what is sufficient for you, that you may not take too much of it and have to vomit it up.

17246.label: Proverbs 25:17
17246.text: Make your foot rare at the house of your fellowman, that he may not have his sufficiency of you and certainly hate you.

17247.label: Proverbs 25:18
17247.text: As a war club and a sword and a sharpened arrow is a man testifying against his fellowman as a false witness.

17248.label: Proverbs 25:19
17248.text: As a broken tooth and a wobbling foot is the confidence in one proving treacherous in the day of distress.

17249.label: Proverbs 25:20
17249.text: He that is removing a garment on a cold day is as vinegar upon alkali and as a singer with songs upon a gloomy heart.

17250.label: Proverbs 25:21
17250.text: If the one hating you is hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.

17251.label: Proverbs 25:22
17251.text: For coals are what you are raking together upon his head, and Jehovah himself will reward you.

17252.label: Proverbs 25:23
17252.text: The wind from the north brings forth as with labor pains a downpour; and a tongue [giving away] a secret, a denounced face.

17253.label: Proverbs 25:24
17253.text: Better is it to dwell upon a corner of a roof than with a contentious wife, although in a house in common.

17254.label: Proverbs 25:25
17254.text: As cold water upon a tired soul, so is a good report from a distant land.

17255.label: Proverbs 25:26
17255.text: A fouled spring and a ruined well is the righteous one when staggering before the wicked one.

17256.label: Proverbs 25:27
17256.text: The eating of too much honey is not good; and for people to search out their own glory, is it glory?

17257.label: Proverbs 25:28
17257.text: As a city broken through, without a wall, is the man that has no restraint for his spirit.

17258.label: Proverbs 26:1
17258.text: Like snow in summer and like rain in harvesttime, so glory is not fitting for a stupid one.

17259.label: Proverbs 26:2
17259.text: Just as a bird has cause for fleeing [and] just as a swallow for flying, so a malediction itself does not come without real cause.

17260.label: Proverbs 26:3
17260.text: A whip is for the horse, a bridle is for the ass, and the rod is for the back of stupid people.

17261.label: Proverbs 26:4
17261.text: Do not answer anyone stupid according to his foolishness, that you yourself also may not become equal to him.

17262.label: Proverbs 26:5
17262.text: Answer someone stupid according to his foolishness, that he may not become someone wise in his own eyes.

17263.label: Proverbs 26:6
17263.text: As one that is mutilating [his] feet, as one that is drinking mere violence, is he that is thrusting matters into the hand of someone stupid.

17264.label: Proverbs 26:7
17264.text: Have the legs of the lame one drawn up water? Then there is a proverb in the mouth of stupid people.

17265.label: Proverbs 26:8
17265.text: Like one shutting up a stone in a heap of stones, so is the one giving glory to a mere stupid one.

17266.label: Proverbs 26:9
17266.text: As a thorny weed has come up into the hand of a drunkard, so a proverb into the mouth of stupid people.

17267.label: Proverbs 26:10
17267.text: As an archer piercing everything is the one hiring someone stupid or the one hiring passersby.

17268.label: Proverbs 26:11
17268.text: Just like a dog returning to its vomit, the stupid one is repeating his foolishness.

17269.label: Proverbs 26:12
17269.text: Have you seen a man wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for the stupid one than for him.

17270.label: Proverbs 26:13
17270.text: The lazy one has said: “There is a young lion in the way, a lion in among the public squares.”

17271.label: Proverbs 26:14
17271.text: A door keeps turning upon its pivot, and the lazy one upon his couch.

17272.label: Proverbs 26:15
17272.text: The lazy one has hidden his hand in the banquet bowl; he has become too weary to bring it back to his mouth.

17273.label: Proverbs 26:16
17273.text: The lazy one is wiser in his own eyes than seven giving a sensible reply.

17274.label: Proverbs 26:17
17274.text: As one grabbing hold of the ears of a dog is anyone passing by that is becoming furious at the quarrel that is not his.

17275.label: Proverbs 26:18
17275.text: Just like someone mad that is shooting fiery missiles, arrows and death,

17276.label: Proverbs 26:19
17276.text: so is the man that has tricked his fellowman and has said: “Was I not having fun?”

17277.label: Proverbs 26:20
17277.text: Where there is no wood the fire goes out, and where there is no slanderer contention grows still.

17278.label: Proverbs 26:21
17278.text: As charcoal for the embers and wood for the fire, so is a contentious man for causing a quarrel to glow.

17279.label: Proverbs 26:22
17279.text: The words of a slanderer are like things to be swallowed greedily, which do go down into the innermost parts of the belly.

17280.label: Proverbs 26:23
17280.text: As a silver glazing overlaid upon a fragment of earthenware are fervent lips along with a bad heart.

17281.label: Proverbs 26:24
17281.text: With his lips the hater makes himself unrecognizable, but inside of him he puts deception.

17282.label: Proverbs 26:25
17282.text: Although he makes his voice gracious, do not believe in him, for there are seven detestable things in his heart.

17283.label: Proverbs 26:26
17283.text: Hatred is covered over by deceit. His badness will be uncovered in the congregation.

17284.label: Proverbs 26:27
17284.text: He that is excavating a pit will fall into the same, and he that is rolling away a stone—back to him it will return.

17285.label: Proverbs 26:28
17285.text: A tongue that is false hates the one crushed by it, and a flattering mouth causes an overthrow.

17286.label: Proverbs 27:1
17286.text: Do not make your boast about the next day, for you do not know what a day will give birth to.

17287.label: Proverbs 27:2
17287.text: May a stranger, and not your own mouth, praise you; may a foreigner, and not your own lips, do so.

17288.label: Proverbs 27:3
17288.text: The heaviness of a stone and a load of sand —but the vexation by someone foolish is heavier than both of them.

17289.label: Proverbs 27:4
17289.text: There is the cruelty of rage, also the flood of anger, but who can stand before jealousy?

17290.label: Proverbs 27:5
17290.text: Better is a revealed reproof than a concealed love.

17291.label: Proverbs 27:6
17291.text: The wounds inflicted by a lover are faithful, but the kisses of a hater are things to be entreated.

17292.label: Proverbs 27:7
17292.text: A soul that is satisfied will tread down comb honey, but to a hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.

17293.label: Proverbs 27:8
17293.text: Just like a bird fleeing away from its nest, so is a man fleeing away from his place.

17294.label: Proverbs 27:9
17294.text: Oil and incense are what make the heart rejoice, also the sweetness of one’s companion due to the counsel of the soul.

17295.label: Proverbs 27:10
17295.text: Do not leave your own companion or the companion of your father, and do not enter the house of your own brother on the day of your disaster. Better is a neighbor that is near than a brother that is far away.

17296.label: Proverbs 27:11
17296.text: Be wise, my son, and make my heart rejoice, that I may make a reply to him that is taunting me.

17297.label: Proverbs 27:12
17297.text: The shrewd one that has seen the calamity has concealed himself; the inexperienced that have passed along have suffered the penalty.

17298.label: Proverbs 27:13
17298.text: Take one’s garment, in case one has gone surety for a stranger; and in the instance of a foreign woman, seize from him a pledge.

17299.label: Proverbs 27:14
17299.text: He that is blessing his fellowman with a loud voice early in the morning, as a malediction it will be accounted on his part.

17300.label: Proverbs 27:15
17300.text: A leaking roof that drives one away in the day of a steady rain and a contentious wife are comparable.

17301.label: Proverbs 27:16
17301.text: Anyone sheltering her has sheltered the wind, and oil is what his right hand encounters.

17302.label: Proverbs 27:17
17302.text: By iron, iron itself is sharpened. So one man sharpens the face of another.

17303.label: Proverbs 27:18
17303.text: He that is safeguarding the fig tree will himself eat its fruit, and he that is guarding his master will be honored.

17304.label: Proverbs 27:19
17304.text: As in water face corresponds with face, so the heart of a man with [that of] a man.

17305.label: Proverbs 27:20
17305.text: Sheʹol and [the place of] destruction themselves do not get satisfied; neither do the eyes of a man get satisfied.

17306.label: Proverbs 27:21
17306.text: The refining pot is for silver, and the furnace is for gold; and an individual is according to his praise.

17307.label: Proverbs 27:22
17307.text: Even if you should pound the foolish one fine with a pestle in a mortar, in among cracked grain, his foolishness will not depart from him.

17308.label: Proverbs 27:23
17308.text: You ought to know positively the appearance of your flock. Set your heart to your droves;

17309.label: Proverbs 27:24
17309.text: for treasure will not be to time indefinite, nor a diadem for all generations.

17310.label: Proverbs 27:25
17310.text: The green grass has departed, and the new grass has appeared, and the vegetation of the mountains has been gathered.

17311.label: Proverbs 27:26
17311.text: The young rams are for your clothing, and the he-goats are the price of the field.

17312.label: Proverbs 27:27
17312.text: And there is a sufficiency of goats’ milk for your food, for the food of your household, and the means of life for your girls.

17313.label: Proverbs 28:1
17313.text: The wicked do flee when there is no pursuer, but the righteous are like a young lion that is confident.

17314.label: Proverbs 28:2
17314.text: Because of the transgression of a land many are its [successive] princes, but by a discerning man having knowledge of right [the prince] will remain long.

17315.label: Proverbs 28:3
17315.text: An able-bodied man that is of little means and that is defrauding the lowly ones is as a rain that washes away so that there is no food.

17316.label: Proverbs 28:4
17316.text: Those who are leaving the law praise the wicked one, but those who are keeping the law excite themselves against them.

17317.label: Proverbs 28:5
17317.text: Men given to badness cannot understand judgment, but those who are seeking Jehovah can understand everything.

17318.label: Proverbs 28:6
17318.text: Better is the one of little means who is walking in his integrity than anyone crooked in [his] ways, although he is rich.

17319.label: Proverbs 28:7
17319.text: An understanding son is observing the law, but one having companionship with gluttons humiliates his father.

17320.label: Proverbs 28:8
17320.text: He that is multiplying his valuables by interest and usury collects them merely for the one showing favor to the lowly ones.

17321.label: Proverbs 28:9
17321.text: He that is turning his ear away from hearing the law —even his prayer is something detestable.

17322.label: Proverbs 28:10
17322.text: He that is causing the upright ones to go astray into the bad way will himself fall into his own pit, but the faultless ones themselves will come into possession of good.

17323.label: Proverbs 28:11
17323.text: A rich man is wise in his own eyes, but the lowly one who is discerning searches him through.

17324.label: Proverbs 28:12
17324.text: When the righteous ones are exulting, there is abundant beauty; but when the wicked ones rise up, a man disguises himself.

17325.label: Proverbs 28:13
17325.text: He that is covering over his transgressions will not succeed, but he that is confessing and leaving [them] will be shown mercy.

17326.label: Proverbs 28:14
17326.text: Happy is the man that is feeling dread constantly, but he that is hardening his heart will fall into calamity.

17327.label: Proverbs 28:15
17327.text: As a growling lion and an onrushing bear is a wicked ruler over a lowly people.

17328.label: Proverbs 28:16
17328.text: A leader that is in want of true discernment is also abundant in fraudulent practices, but he that is hating unjust profit will prolong [his] days.

17329.label: Proverbs 28:17
17329.text: A man burdened with the bloodguilt for a soul will himself flee even to the pit. Let them not get hold of him.

17330.label: Proverbs 28:18
17330.text: He that is walking faultless will be saved, but he that is made crooked in [his] ways will fall at once.

17331.label: Proverbs 28:19
17331.text: He that is cultivating his own ground will have his sufficiency of bread, and he that is pursuing valueless things will have his sufficiency of poverty.

17332.label: Proverbs 28:20
17332.text: A man of faithful acts will get many blessings, but he that is hastening to gain riches will not remain innocent.

17333.label: Proverbs 28:21
17333.text: The showing of partiality is not good, nor that an able-bodied man should transgress over a mere piece of bread.

17334.label: Proverbs 28:22
17334.text: A man of envious eye is bestirring himself after valuable things, but he does not know that want itself will come upon him.

17335.label: Proverbs 28:23
17335.text: He that is reproving a man will afterward find more favor than he will that is flattering with his tongue.

17336.label: Proverbs 28:24
17336.text: He that is robbing his father and his mother and is saying: “It is no transgression,” is a partner of a man causing ruination.

17337.label: Proverbs 28:25
17337.text: He that is arrogant in soul stirs up contention, but he that is relying upon Jehovah will be made fat.

17338.label: Proverbs 28:26
17338.text: He that is trusting in his own heart is stupid, but he that is walking in wisdom is the one that will escape.

17339.label: Proverbs 28:27
17339.text: He that is giving to the one of little means will have no want, but he that is hiding his eyes will get many curses.

17340.label: Proverbs 28:28
17340.text: When the wicked rise up, a man conceals himself; but when they perish, the righteous become many.

17341.label: Proverbs 29:1
17341.text: A man repeatedly reproved but making his neck hard will suddenly be broken, and that without healing.

17342.label: Proverbs 29:2
17342.text: When the righteous become many, the people rejoice; but when anyone wicked bears rule, the people sigh.

17343.label: Proverbs 29:3
17343.text: A man that is loving wisdom makes his father rejoice, but he that is having companionship with prostitutes destroys valuable things.

17344.label: Proverbs 29:4
17344.text: By justice a king makes a land keep standing, but a man out for bribes tears it down.

17345.label: Proverbs 29:5
17345.text: An able-bodied man that is flattering his companion is spreading out a mere net for his steps.

17346.label: Proverbs 29:6
17346.text: In the transgression of a bad man there is a snare, but he that is righteous cries out joyfully and is glad.

17347.label: Proverbs 29:7
17347.text: The righteous one is knowing the legal claim of the lowly ones. He that is wicked does not consider such knowledge.

17348.label: Proverbs 29:8
17348.text: Men of boastful talk inflame a town, but those who are wise turn back anger.

17349.label: Proverbs 29:9
17349.text: A wise man having entered into judgment with a foolish man—he has become excited and has also laughed, and there is no rest.

17350.label: Proverbs 29:10
17350.text: Bloodthirsty men hate anyone blameless; and as for the upright ones, they keep seeking for the soul of each one.

17351.label: Proverbs 29:11
17351.text: All his spirit is what a stupid one lets out, but he that is wise keeps it calm to the last.

17352.label: Proverbs 29:12
17352.text: Where a ruler is paying attention to false speech, all those waiting on him will be wicked.

17353.label: Proverbs 29:13
17353.text: The one of little means and the man of oppressions have met each other; [but] Jehovah is lighting up the eyes of them both.

17354.label: Proverbs 29:14
17354.text: Where a king is judging the lowly ones in trueness, his throne will be firmly established for all time.

17355.label: Proverbs 29:15
17355.text: The rod and reproof are what give wisdom; but a boy let on the loose will be causing his mother shame.

17356.label: Proverbs 29:16
17356.text: When the wicked become many, transgression abounds; but those who are righteous will look on their very downfall.

17357.label: Proverbs 29:17
17357.text: Chastise your son and he will bring you rest and give much pleasure to your soul.

17358.label: Proverbs 29:18
17358.text: Where there is no vision the people go unrestrained, but happy are they that are keeping the law.

17359.label: Proverbs 29:19
17359.text: A servant will not let himself be corrected by mere words, for he understands but he is paying no heed.

17360.label: Proverbs 29:20
17360.text: Have you beheld a man hasty with his words? There is more hope for someone stupid than for him.

17361.label: Proverbs 29:21
17361.text: If one is pampering one’s servant from youth on, in his later life he will even become a thankless one.

17362.label: Proverbs 29:22
17362.text: A man given to anger stirs up contention, and anyone disposed to rage has many a transgression.

17363.label: Proverbs 29:23
17363.text: The very haughtiness of earthling man will humble him, but he that is humble in spirit will take hold of glory.

17364.label: Proverbs 29:24
17364.text: He that is partner with a thief is hating his own soul. An oath involving a curse he may hear, but he reports nothing.

17365.label: Proverbs 29:25
17365.text: Trembling at men is what lays a snare, but he that is trusting in Jehovah will be protected.

17366.label: Proverbs 29:26
17366.text: Many are those seeking the face of a ruler, but the judgment of a man is from Jehovah.

17367.label: Proverbs 29:27
17367.text: A man of injustice is something detestable to the righteous ones, and one who is upright in his way is something detestable to a wicked one.

17368.label: Proverbs 30:1
17368.text: The words of Aʹgur the son of Jaʹkeh, the weighty message. The utterance of the able-bodied man to Ithʹi·el, to Ithʹi·el and Uʹcal.

17369.label: Proverbs 30:2
17369.text: For I am more unreasoning than anyone else, and I do not have the understanding of mankind;

17370.label: Proverbs 30:3
17370.text: and I have not learned wisdom; and the knowledge of the Most Holy One I do not know.

17371.label: Proverbs 30:4
17371.text: Who has ascended to heaven that he may descend? Who has gathered the wind in the hollow of both hands? Who has wrapped up the waters in a mantle? Who has made all the ends of the earth to rise? What is his name and what the name of his son, in case you know?

17372.label: Proverbs 30:5
17372.text: Every saying of God is refined. He is a shield to those taking refuge in him.

17373.label: Proverbs 30:6
17373.text: Add nothing to his words, that he may not reprove you, and that you may not have to be proved a liar.

17374.label: Proverbs 30:7
17374.text: Two things I have asked of you. Do not withhold them from me before I die.

17375.label: Proverbs 30:8
17375.text: Untruth and the lying word put far away from me. Give me neither poverty nor riches. Let me devour the food prescribed for me,

17376.label: Proverbs 30:9
17376.text: that I may not become satisfied and I actually deny [you] and say: “Who is Jehovah?” and that I may not come to poverty and I actually steal and assail the name of my God.

17377.label: Proverbs 30:10
17377.text: Do not slander a servant to his master, that he may not call down evil upon you, and that you may not have to be held guilty.

17378.label: Proverbs 30:11
17378.text: There is a generation that calls down evil even upon its father and that does not bless even its mother.

17379.label: Proverbs 30:12
17379.text: There is a generation that is pure in its own eyes but that has not been washed from its own excrement.

17380.label: Proverbs 30:13
17380.text: There is a generation whose eyes have become O how lofty! and whose beaming eyes are lifted up.

17381.label: Proverbs 30:14
17381.text: There is a generation whose teeth are swords and whose jawbones are slaughtering knives, to eat up the afflicted ones off the earth and the poor ones from among mankind.

17382.label: Proverbs 30:15
17382.text: The leeches have two daughters [that cry]: “Give! Give!” There are three things that do not get satisfied, four that have not said: “Enough!”

17383.label: Proverbs 30:16
17383.text: Sheʹol and a restrained womb, a land that has not been satisfied with water, and fire that has not said: “Enough!”

17384.label: Proverbs 30:17
17384.text: The eye that holds a father in derision and that despises obedience to a mother —the ravens of the torrent valley will pick it out and the sons of the eagle will eat it up.

17385.label: Proverbs 30:18
17385.text: There are three things that have proved too wonderful for me, and four that I have not come to know:

17386.label: Proverbs 30:19
17386.text: the way of an eagle in the heavens, the way of a serpent on a rock, the way of a ship in the heart of the sea and the way of an able-bodied man with a maiden.

17387.label: Proverbs 30:20
17387.text: Here is the way of an adulterous woman: she has eaten and has wiped her mouth and she has said: “I have committed no wrong.”

17388.label: Proverbs 30:21
17388.text: Under three things the earth has been agitated, and under four it is not able to endure:

17389.label: Proverbs 30:22
17389.text: under a slave when he rules as king, and someone senseless when he has his sufficiency of food;

17390.label: Proverbs 30:23
17390.text: under a hated woman when she is taken possession of as a wife, and a maidservant when she dispossesses her mistress.

17391.label: Proverbs 30:24
17391.text: There are four things that are the smallest of the earth, but they are instinctively wise:

17392.label: Proverbs 30:25
17392.text: the ants are a people not strong, and yet in the summer they prepare their food;

17393.label: Proverbs 30:26
17393.text: the rock badgers are a people not mighty, and yet upon a crag is where they put their house;

17394.label: Proverbs 30:27
17394.text: the locusts have no king, and yet they go forth all of them divided into groups;

17395.label: Proverbs 30:28
17395.text: the gecko lizard takes hold with its own hands and it is in the grand palace of a king.

17396.label: Proverbs 30:29
17396.text: There are three that do well in [their] pacing, and four that do well in [their] moving along:

17397.label: Proverbs 30:30
17397.text: the lion, which is the mightiest among the beasts and which does not turn back from before anyone;

17398.label: Proverbs 30:31
17398.text: the greyhound or the he-goat, and a king of a band of soldiers of his own people.

17399.label: Proverbs 30:32
17399.text: If you have acted senselessly by lifting yourself up, and if you have fixed your thought [upon it], [put] the hand to the mouth.

17400.label: Proverbs 30:33
17400.text: For the churning of milk is what brings forth butter, and the squeezing of the nose is what brings forth blood, and the squeezing out of anger is what brings forth quarreling.

17401.label: Proverbs 31:1
17401.text: The words of Lemʹu·el the king, the weighty message that his mother gave to him in correction:

17402.label: Proverbs 31:2
17402.text: What [am I saying], O son of mine, and what, O son of my belly, and what, O son of my vows?

17403.label: Proverbs 31:3
17403.text: Do not give your vital energy to women, nor your ways to [what leads to] wiping out kings.

17404.label: Proverbs 31:4
17404.text: It is not for kings, O Lemʹu·el, it is not for kings to drink wine or for high officials [to say:] “Where is intoxicating liquor?”

17405.label: Proverbs 31:5
17405.text: that one may not drink and forget what is decreed and pervert the cause of any of the sons of affliction.

17406.label: Proverbs 31:6
17406.text: Give intoxicating liquor, YOU people, to the one about to perish and wine to those who are bitter of soul.

17407.label: Proverbs 31:7
17407.text: Let one drink and forget one’s poverty, and let one remember one’s own trouble no more.

17408.label: Proverbs 31:8
17408.text: Open your mouth for the speechless one, in the cause of all those passing away.

17409.label: Proverbs 31:9
17409.text: Open your mouth, judge righteously and plead the cause of the afflicted one and the poor one.

17410.label: Proverbs 31:10
17410.text: A capable wife who can find? Her value is far more than that of corals.

17411.label: Proverbs 31:11
17411.text: In her the heart of her owner has put trust, and there is no gain lacking.

17412.label: Proverbs 31:12
17412.text: She has rewarded him with good, and not bad, all the days of her life.

17413.label: Proverbs 31:13
17413.text: She has sought wool and linen, and she works at whatever is the delight of her hands.

17414.label: Proverbs 31:14
17414.text: She has proved to be like the ships of a merchant. From far away she brings in her food.

17415.label: Proverbs 31:15
17415.text: She also gets up while it is still night, and gives food to her household and the prescribed portion to her young women.

17416.label: Proverbs 31:16
17416.text: She has considered a field and proceeded to obtain it; from the fruitage of her hands she has planted a vineyard.

17417.label: Proverbs 31:17
17417.text: She has girded her hips with strength, and she invigorates her arms.

17418.label: Proverbs 31:18
17418.text: She has sensed that her trading is good; her lamp does not go out at night.

17419.label: Proverbs 31:19
17419.text: Her hands she has thrust out to the distaff, and her own hands take hold of the spindle.

17420.label: Proverbs 31:20
17420.text: Her palm she has stretched out to the afflicted one, and her hands she has thrust out to the poor one.

17421.label: Proverbs 31:21
17421.text: She does not fear for her household because of the snow, for all her household are clothed with double garments.

17422.label: Proverbs 31:22
17422.text: Coverlets she has made for herself. Her clothing is of linen and wool dyed reddish purple.

17423.label: Proverbs 31:23
17423.text: Her owner is someone known in the gates, when he sits down with the older men of the land.

17424.label: Proverbs 31:24
17424.text: She has made even undergarments and proceeded to sell [them], and belts she has given to the tradesmen.

17425.label: Proverbs 31:25
17425.text: Strength and splendor are her clothing, and she laughs at a future day.

17426.label: Proverbs 31:26
17426.text: Her mouth she has opened in wisdom, and the law of loving-kindness is upon her tongue.

17427.label: Proverbs 31:27
17427.text: She is watching over the goings-on of her household, and the bread of laziness she does not eat.

17428.label: Proverbs 31:28
17428.text: Her sons have risen up and proceeded to pronounce her happy; her owner [rises up], and he praises her.

17429.label: Proverbs 31:29
17429.text: There are many daughters that have shown capableness, but you—you have ascended above them all.

17430.label: Proverbs 31:30
17430.text: Charm may be false, and prettiness may be vain; [but] the woman that fears Jehovah is the one that procures praise for herself.

17431.label: Proverbs 31:31
17431.text: GIVE her of the fruitage of her hands, and let her works praise her even in the gates.
